#119921. Breaking: Connor Hellebuyck trade: Jets send star goalie to the Devils in exchange for four players, two draft picks

Breaking: Connor Hellebuyck trade: Jets send star goalie to the Devils in exchange for four players, two draft picks

📅 24 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1136 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The star goalie for the Winnipeg Jets is on the move after being traded to Newly introduced Jersey on Friday in exchange for four players and two future draft picks.
  • According to recent reports, hellebuyck expressed his desire to be traded in the offseason when he formally requested a move in August.
  • Hellebuyck has spent his entire career with Winnipeg after being drafted by the Jets in 2012 at No.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Connor Hellebuyck is a now a Devil. The star goalie for the Winnipeg Jets is on the move after being traded to Newly introduced Jersey on Friday in exchange for four players and two future draft picks. the teams announced the move with the Jets receiving Dawson Mercer, Nick Bjugstad, Nico Daws and Alexander Command, plus a 2027 seventh-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick.

According to recent reports, hellebuyck expressed his desire to be traded in the offseason when he formally requested a move in August. He remarked at the time that he had made the request months earlier and tried to keep the situation private.

Hellebuyck has spent his entire career with Winnipeg after being drafted by the Jets in 2012 at No. 130 overall. He's recognized as one of the best goalies in the league as a three-time Vezina Trophy winner. He also helped carry the United States to its first gold medal since 1980 at the 2026 Olympics in February with some incredible saves against Canada in the final game.

In a recent development, after trading Jacob Markstom in the offseason, the Devils had a clear need in goal, and this splashy move certainly fills that need. With a talented young core already in place, Upcoming Jersey's Stanley Cup window is wide open.

RAISE HELLE!Connor Hellebuyck is a Upcoming Jersey Devil: https://t.co/HCehRGOQI5 pic.twitter.com/dZGNQR16m1.

In a recent development, for the Jets, it must be a hard pill to swallow when a franchise icon decides to walk out they door, but this trade package should help them as the enter a new era and revamp the roster. Winnipeg got a former first-rounder in Mercer to try and add to a rebuild as well as a veteran presence in Bjugstad. They also acquired a younger goalie in Daws who could fill the role of Hellebuyck at just 25 years old.

Goaltending has been an problem in Upcoming Jersey for a while now -- even after the team acquired Markstrom from the Calgary Flames in 2024. Markstom never really panned out, and his 13.6 goals allowed above average, per Natural Stat Trick, were a substantial reason why the Devils missed the postseason last year.

In the early portion of this season, it was clear that Upcoming Jersey needed to make a move to upgrade in the crease. Daws and veteran Jake Allen simply aren't a tandem suitable for a Stanley Cup contender, and the numbers backed that up. New Jersey ranks 24th in team save percentage at .877, and the duo of Daws and Allen combined to surrender 2.99 goals above average.

Once Hellebuyck gets up to game speed, that shouldn't be a problem anymore.

In the three-season stretch from 2023-26, Hellebuyck led the NHL with 73.42 goals saved above average, which is 20 goals higher than the next closest netminder. Over that span, Hellebuyck also posted a standard save percentage of .914 and an astronomical high-danger save-percentage of .832.

In a recent development, hellebuyck carried less talented teams to the playoffs multiple times in his career. Now on a team loaded with weaponry in their prime -- Jack Hughes, Jesper Bratt and Nico Hischier to name a few -- Hellebuyck could be the final piece to the championship puzzle.

In terms of the acquisition cost, it was probably an easy deal for Devils general manager Sunny Mehta to make. The 2029 second-round pick is useless for a team that should be all-in now, Bjugstad is simply a depth piece and Daws now has no path to a starting role with Hellebuyck in town.

According to recent reports, the most interesting trade chips are Mercer and Command. Mercer flashed major upside with 56 points in his second NHL season, 2022-23, but he hasn't really come close to hitting those heights again. Still, even if he has plateaued, Mercer remains a strong middle-six forward rising into his prime.

Although Command had his detractors -- and may have been over-drafted at No. 12 overall -- he was a consensus first-round pick last summer. That gives Winnipeg a potential franchise forward it can build around long-term, but Upcoming Jersey already has one of the deepest forward groups in the league, especially with the emergence of Arseny Gritsyuk and the acquisition of Luke Evangelista.

Sources indicate that if we're looking for a 3-D chess angle of this deal, it only makes the Devils more appealing for a certain Minnesota Wild defenseman whose brothers just happen to play in Upcoming Jersey already. Grade -- A+.

Let's get the obvious out of the way first: The Jets were never going to get fair value for Hellebuyck because, at his best, he's the No. 1 goaltender in the world with no equal. That type of excellence can't be replaced.

That remarked, Winnipeg did fairly well given the circumstances. Hellebuyck made a public trade request, and he wasn't even with the team after sitting out for the entirety of training camp. The entire league knew the Jets had to trade him.

Hellebuyck's talent created a decent market anyway, but most of the suitors were bona fide Stanley Cup contenders with little in the way of valuable draft capital, and they weren't going to knee cap the roster by sending a key player back in return.

With all that taken into consideration, Kevin Cheveldayoff got a solid return. Although Mercer's ceiling may be lower than initially thought, he's a 24-year-old forward who banks roughly 20 goals and 20 assists every season. The kicker with Mercer will be Winnipeg's ability to re-sign him before he hits restricted free agency next summer.

Recent findings suggest that the addition of Command means Winnipeg now has two forwards selected in the top 12 of the 2026 NHL Draft after taking center Viggo Bjorck themselves. If both of those players deliver on their first-round pedigrees, they could be a terrific one-two punch for the team long-term.

Recent findings suggest that daws was a third-round pick in 2020, and despite playing just 13 NHL games since the start of the 2024-25 season, he should give Winnipeg a solid back up option behind Stuart Skinner. It certainly helps that Skinner is off to a great start with his upcoming team -- and if Daws develops into a true No. 1 -- it'll be gravy.

If there's any reason to critique this deal from the Jets' side of things, it's that they didn't get premium draft capital or a surefire up-and-coming prospect. Maybe Command develops into a star, but there's no guarantee he becomes a top-six stud in the NHL.

The Jets got a lot of good stuff, but they didn't really get anything great, at least not based on what we know in the moment. Because of that, I have to ding Winnipeg a little bit. Grade: B.

NBA's eight biggest disappointments through one month: Injury bug, same old East and an underwhelming champ

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1749 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, we're roughly one month into the 2026-27 NBA season, and things are going pretty well in certain respects.
  • Recent findings suggest that in other areas, things are going … not so well.
  • There have been so many players impacted by various injuries that it's almost hard to keep track.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, we're roughly one month into the 2026-27 NBA season, and things are going pretty well in certain respects. Luka Dončić and the Lakers are off to a hot start in Los Angeles. Victor Wembanyama and the Spurs have picked up right where they left off after last season's Finals trip. And the Celtics are battling the latest-look Sixers at the top of the Eastern Conference.

Recent findings suggest that in other areas, things are going … not so well. Below are the eight biggest disappointments so far this season.

There have been so many players impacted by various injuries that it's almost hard to keep track. Jalen Duren (hamstring) has missed almost the entire season in Detroit. Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody are still recovering from knee injuries and have yet to play for Golden State, while Steph Curry is now out with an abdominal tear and Kristaps Porziņģis stepped away from basketball. After sitting out all of last season with an Achilles tear, Tyrese Haliburton is presently dealing with a hamstring issue. Brandon Ingram (Achilles) hasn't made his debut for the Clippers. Austin Reaves is out with a heel injury. Anthony Edwards underwent knee surgery and will miss a chunk of time for the Wolves, and it seems unlikely that Donte DiVincenzo (Achilles) will play this season, even though he remains hopeful that he will. Paolo Banchero remains sidelined with an ankle sprain. Ja Morant is out with a hamstring strain. Ben Simmons didn't play a single game for the Kings before tearing his Achilles. Kawhi Leonard (knee) is once again on the shelf in Toronto. And the reeling Jazz are without Jaren Jackson Jr (knee), Lauri Markkanen (hand) and Jusuf Nurkic (toe).

Recent findings suggest that it's all a huge bummer for the players, their teams and fans of hoops in general. But no team has been hurt more on the injury front than the Thunder.

The disappointment here is how unkind fate has been to OKC. The Thunder were close to fully healthy when the season started — and then far from it not long after it began. When OKC beat the Spurs in San Antonio in the season opener — after losing four of five regular season games to them last season, as well as falling to the Spurs in the Western Conference Finals — it felt like a statement that the Thunder were back and we were in for an epic battle between the two teams over who would rule the West.

And then all of that was stripped away. Just three games into the season, Jalen Williams — who missed much of last season due to injury — suffered a gruesome fall and had to undergo surgery for a fractured fibula as well as reconstruction of ankle ligaments. In that same fateful game, Cason Wallace tore his labrum and later had shoulder surgery. They haven't been officially ruled out, but if either of them plays basketball again this season, it will be a surprise. Making matters worse, Chet Holmgren tore a tendon in his knee and "underwent a biological treatment" to address it. He'll miss approximately two months, but the Thunder do expect him to return. That's what passes for good news in OKC these days.

Recent findings suggest that the Thunder are — or were — the deepest team in the NBA. That's a credit to what Sam Presti built. But even OKC has its limits. Losing three of five starters is tough to overcome, even when you're led by the reigning back-to-back MVP in Shai Gilgeous-Alexander. That doesn't mean the Thunder (at the moment 9-6 and eighth in the West) can't still make a deep playoff run, but the odds of them doing so — and of them fighting the Spurs all season for the top spot — got a lot longer.

Sources indicate that we were told that this was finally the season that the East returned to its former glory. We were told that the conference would be loaded. We were wrong. (Full disclosure while putting a palm to my face: I might have done some of that telling.).

Recent findings suggest that through the first month, the East has been mostly underwhelming. Eight of the 15 teams are below .500. The conference has a combined 17-37 record against the West. Only one of the top seven teams in net rating — the Celtics — plays in the East. Five of the top six teams by point differential play in the West.

Industry observers note that the defending champion Knicks are 8-6. The Cavaliers, who made it to last season's Eastern Conference Finals and had championship aspirations of their own, are 8-8. The Magic, Raptors and Pacers — who currently occupy the eight, nine and 10 seeds — all have losing records. By contrast, the worst play-in team in the West right now is Golden State at 8-7. That record would be good enough for the seven seed if they played in the East.

But maybe we shouldn't be surprised. Since the 1999-2000 season, the West has had the better overall record in all but three campaigns. Maybe next year the East will finally snap out of its funk, but don't bet on it.

Recent findings suggest that the Jazz just picked up back-to-back road wins in L.A. over the Lakers and Clippers, but that doesn't begin to dig them out of the deep hole they've made for themselves. The Jazz were gearing up to be competitive in the West this season. So much for that. Like the Thunder, injuries have not been kind to them. Nurkic has yet to play a single game this season, while Markkanen and JJJ have missed significant time with maladies of their own. What looked like a formidable frontcourt has been decimated.

Still, it's hard to believe how bad the Jazz have been in pretty much every facet. Their first win came in the second game of the season, a one-point squeaker over the Pelicans. It took until mid-November to end an ugly 12-game losing streak and pick up their second and third wins. They're 25th in net rating and point differential. The season has barely begun, and it's already basically wait until next year for the Jazz.

It has been revealed that the NBA panicked and tried to solve for a problem that wasn't actually an glitch, except for a small fragment of people who care more about optics than the product itself. And so the league enacted lottery reform and the new 3-2-1 system was put in place. This was ostensibly designed to prevent tanking, incentivize winning and bring greater parity to the league. Oops.

In a recent development, the Hornets, Wizards, Bulls, Nets and Bucks are all well underwater in the East. The Pelicans and Clippers are drowning in the West, while the Kings and Jazz are even worse. What the league failed to account for is that some of these teams are just organically bad — and now they will have decreased odds at getting better.

Sources indicate that under the old system, the Grizzlies would be pretty thrilled to see the Jazz struggling since Memphis has Utah's first-round pick in the upcoming draft as part of the JJJ trade. Alas, after making that move, the league changed the rules, which means the Grizzlies can pick no higher than sixth now as a consequence of the new system preventing a team from picking in the top five in three consecutive drafts. Since the Jazz picked in the top five in each of the last two drafts, that means the Grizzlies are now out of luck with that Utah pick this time around. Womp, womp for them.

And on top of it all, fans of bad teams were robbed of the entertaining-in-its-own-way race to the bottom to maximize lottery odds, giving supporters a small silver lining in the otherwise gray clouds of their season. RIP Tank Watch.

When aren't the Kings disappointing? Aside from their unsightly 1-13 record, the Sacramento front office continues to make baffling decisions. The Kings originally acquired Nique Clifford from the Thunder for a Spurs 2027 first-round pick. Sacramento held onto Clifford for 83 games — choosing to bury him on the bench this season and play him barely six minutes per game — before shipping him back to the Thunder for two second-round picks.

So the Thunder ended up with the player and a first and the Kings ended up with two seconds.

One of these organizations is savvy and opportunistic, and the other is the Kings. It's a miracle they nailed the Darius Acuff pick.

Oof. It has not been a good season to date for Bridges. After going cold to begin their first-round playoff series against the Hawks, Bridges found his form and played well, helping the Knicks go on an epic run that ended with New York's first championship in 53 years.

If that hope was that Bridges would snap out of his early-season funk in similar fashion, the Knicks seem somewhat less patient these days. While head coach Mike Brown has insisted that Bridges is a starter, he has sometimes hedged his bets in crucial situations, going with Landry Shamet or Deuce McBride over Bridges when things get tight and the Knicks need more reliable offense on the floor.

Through 14 games, Bridges is averaging 7.5 points, 3.6 rebounds and 2.1 assists on 40.2/28.9/75 shooting splits. It's the lowest scoring output and the worst shooting numbers of his career. As a result, his minutes have dipped to 25.6 per contest. That's also a career low. Bridges is still a plus defender. And he's only 30. The Knicks obviously hope he'll figure it out, as he has in the past. If not, his new four-year, $150 million extension that kicked in this season will start to look worrisome.

Why are we still subjected to … [motions at everything below in the most pejorative fashion possible] ... this?

ALL 30 TEAM COURTS FOR @EMIRATES NBA CUP 2026 pic.twitter.com/RgBqe1VJCB.

Why can't whoever came up with the gorgeous GTA VI crossover court in Miami be in charge of the Cup floors instead?

The Miami Heat are rolling out the “Vice City” hardwood 😮‍💨👏(via @MiamiHEAT) pic.twitter.com/AFcyK2akaV.

In a recent development, respecting the Cup would be so much easier if they'd give us more of this. Maybe they could dream up some sweet latest jerseys while they're at it.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The 2026-27 NBA season is barely a month old and trade season won't officially begin until December 15 when players signed this summer are eligible to be moved, but that doesn't stop the rumor machine from churning in the Association.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The 2026-27 NBA season is barely a month old and trade season won't officially begin until December 15 when players signed this summer are eligible to be moved, but that doesn't stop the rumor machine from churning in the Association.

It has been revealed that the first 15 games of the season have been enough for some teams to learn the harsh truth about not being a contender this year, while others are off to surprisingly good starts that could turn them into midseason buyers. That's how the trade market starts to take shape, and with a trade request already made in Upcoming Orleans by Dejounte Murray and a handful of expiring contracts known to be open to moving, we can start piecing together an early look at what trade season may look like.

Industry observers note that the one unknown this season is how the league's lottery reform will affect the in-season trade market. Fewer teams will have incentive to completely bottom out, but even with teams not trying to sell everything off, there will still be enough teams trying to buy to create a market.

On Thursday, we got a fresh batch of rumors, starting with some updates on potential suitors for Murray after being sent home by the Pelicans.

Murray makes $32.8 million this year and has a player option for $30.8 million next year that he will almost assuredly pick up. That means he's not exactly a coveted asset, and even for teams with a potential need at point guard, so far no one seems to be jumping at the opportunity to trade for the disgruntled Pelicans guard.

Two teams that were promptly connected as potential destinations for Murray were the Suns and the Heat, both with glaring point guard needs and a desire to contend this season. However, neither team is desperate to make a move right now, according to Jake Fischer in the latest Stein Line newsletter.

Recent findings suggest that murray and Klutch Sports see Phoenix as a good landing spot, but the Suns view center as a bigger need than point guard and would demand that the Pelicans send back draft capital to take on Murray's salary, Fischer reports. Miami, meanwhile, has shown little appetite for Murray and he is not expected to be one of its trade targets because of his player option for next season that would severely limit their ability to retool the roster around Giannis Antetokounmpo.

With the two most obvious potential suitors for Murray not exactly showing a lot of excitement for bringing him in, it seems likely that Murray's trade request and absence from the Pelicans will extend for quite some time and could last all the way to the trade deadline.

It has been revealed that the Washington Wizards are 5-11 to start the season, which makes it increasingly unlikely they will be trying to work out a long-term extension for Davis. The early returns on Washington's commitment to Trae Young have not been good, and if the Wizards are looking to acquire some assets this season, Davis makes the most sense as an expiring contract.

On the latest episode of the Hoop Collective, ESPN's Brian Windhorst offered an update on Davis' market and desires for his next contract.

Sources indicate that "I think people have demand for Anthony Davis," Windhorst stated. "They just don't want to give him a max extension, and I don't think he's looking for a max extension, but I do think he's looking for a lot of money.".

That's not exactly groundbreaking information and any team exploring a trade for Davis will want to know what, exactly, he's looking for in his next contract. Below the max is a start, but teams are growing wary of giving out massive money to aging stars in the second apron era. Davis brings an additional level of risk to any long-term contract discussions with his injury history.

That stated, he has been quite good this season -- averaging 24.6 points and 10.1 rebounds per game on solid efficiency -- and the Wizards should be shopping him to teams desperate for a center upgrade. If Phoenix is less interested in a point guard but has an appetite for a star center, perhaps the Suns could be a trade partner to offload Jalen Green's contract -- to be clear, that's not a rumor, just connecting dots between a few recent rumors.

Everything with Davis' market will come down to what Davis and Rich Paul tell teams about what they want his next contract to look like.

With Murray on the block and the Pelicans at 5-11, it's fair to wonder (again) if some of Latest Orleans' more intriguing players could find their way onto the trade market.

The player most teams around the league covet in New Orleans is Trey Murphy III. Even though he's in the midst of a slow start to the season and currently dealing with knee tendonitis, other teams still covet his potential as a star on the wing given his abilities as a scorer and defender. The Pelicans also believe strongly in Murphy's upside, and unfortunately for other teams, Fischer reports Murphy -- unlike Murray -- has no desire to make a trade request.

Sources indicate that as such, he's going to be quite expensive to pry from the Pelicans, who "remain reluctant" to discuss trades for Murphy. Given he's their best potential trade chip, that's probably a wise approach, and Newly introduced Orleans will hope some hopeful contender is desperate enough to give up a haul of assets before they consider moving him.

The 30-year-old lefty was 12-7 with a 2.72 ERA and 186 strikeouts in 158 ⅔ innings last season, as he bounced back after just six weeks from elbow surgery.

The teams most heavily involved in the Skubal rumors to this point have been the Dodgers, Mets, Padres and Blue Jays, all of whom had in-person meetings with him last week.

Sources indicate that the Tigers have agreed to a deal with right-hander Luis Gil, per ESPN. It's a one-year, $2.3 million deal.

Gil won the American League Rookie of the Year after a productive 2024 season in which he won 15 games and had a 3.50 ERA, but he spent a good portion of 2026 in the minors and was nontendered by the Yankees on Friday. In his limited MLB time last season, Gil had a 4.61 ERA, 1.43 WHIP and 17 strikeouts in 27 ⅓ innings.

The Tigers rotation seems set with Framber Valdez, Troy Melton, Keider Montero, Jackson Jobe and River Ryan, so consider Gil a depth option.

The Red Sox also reportedly showed interest.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, ace left-hander Tarik Skubal, winner of the last two American League Cy Young awards and far and away the top free agent of the 2026-27 class, has agreed to terms with the New York Mets on a nine-year contract worth $450 million, reports the New York Post. The deal has a $45 million signing bonus with no options or opt-outs, per SNY, as well as a full no-trade clause, so the Mets have locked Skubal up for the full nine years. Further, there are only $30 million in deferrals, according to the New York Post. The deal is pending a physical.

Once finalized, the deal will make Skubal the highest-paid pitcher in Major League Baseball history, in terms of both total contract value and average annual salary.

Skubal, who turned 30 years of age on Nov. 20, is the No. 1 ranked talent on our list of the top 50 free agents for this offseason. Here's part of Mike Axisa's write-up:.

"Excluding Yoshinobu Yamamoto, who was a special case as a Japanese star with no MLB track record, Skubal is the best starting pitcher to hit free agency since Gerrit Cole in 2019. He showed few long-lasting effects from the NanoScope elbow surgery in May and remains a capital-A Ace with terrific surface stats and under-the-hood performance indicators. Skubal brings four swing-and-miss pitches to the table (four-seamer, changeup, slider, curveball), a near MLB-best ability to limit exit velocity, and elite strike-throwing ability (MLB's third-lowest walk rate since 2023). Build an ace starter in a lab and he would look a lot like Skubal. He'll play the entire 2027 season at age 30, and given the things teams can do with pitchers these days, Skubal figures to remain a frontline starter for most of a long-term contract. He's the only true balance-of-power player available in free agency this offseason. Skubal can swing a division race and a postseason series all by himself.".

According to recent reports, over the last three seasons, Skubal has pitched to a 2.42 ERA and an FIP of 2.48 in 546 innings spread over 88 starts. That amounts to a total WAR of 17.7 since the start of the 2024 campaign. Skubal remains foremost in the discussion for best pitcher in baseball, and this signing reflects that reality.

It has been revealed that since Skubal was traded to the Los Angeles Dodgers from the Detroit Tigers leading up to the 2026 deadline, he was ineligible to receive the qualifying offer from the Dodgers. As such, the Mets will not be penalized a draft pick for signing Skubal.

According to recent reports, the nine years here aren't record-setting, as the longest pitcher contract remains the 12-year deal that Yoshinobu Yamamoto signed with the Dodgers. Yamamoto's $325 million was previously the largest contract for a pitcher -- obviously excepting Shohei Ohtani, as he's a two-way player -- so Skubal's $450 million shatters that record.

Coming off a disappointing 88-loss campaign in 2026, the Mets, massive-spending owner Steve Cohen, and lead decision-maker David Stearns needed to make an offseason splash to improve their chances of a 2027 rebound and inspire a perhaps disaffected fan base. Skubal more than qualifies. He'll front a Mets rotation that also includes 25-year-old right-hander Nolan McLean, who himself has frontline long-term potential. In Queens, Skubal joins a roster that also includes the All-Star likes of Juan Soto, Francisco Lindor, and Bo Bichette.

Industry observers note that further, the Mets just locked up young outfielder A.J. Ewing to an eight-year, $95 million extension and we all know plenty about Soto's monster contract. The Mets now have Soto through 2039, Skubal through 2035, Ewing through 2034 and Lindor through 2031.

The rotation for the Mets right now looks something like:.

According to recent reports, given the large outlay for Skubal here, the Mets should be all-in on improving the ballclub for the 2027 season, which means we shouldn't expect them to stop with just signing Skubal. That last spot in the rotation, as such, should be ticketed to someone else outside the organization at present, whether a free agent or a trade acquisition.

The landing of the top free agent available no doubt ramps up the pressure on Stearns and the Mets to deliver a playoff berth and a deep October run in 2027, but Skubal's presence also makes it much likely that such a feat comes to pass.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that when it comes to the holidays, it's best to expect the unexpected. Rarely do things go smoothly when everyone convenes for Thanksgiving, so it's the right idea to lie back and simply roll with the punches as they come in. For instance, you have no idea what that weird uncle will say at the dinner table, nor can you guarantee the turkey won't be overcooked. It's bound to go off the rails in some capacity, but the one constant that you can lean on is that there will be football to help distract you from the madness, including the dog running outside with one of the turkey legs.

Sources indicate that that said, even the NFL is unpredictable, so it's up to us to try and see the forest through the trees and anticipate what could be on the horizon. Below, we're going to highlight a handful of storylines/individual performances from Week 12 that may surprise some people, but not us.

All NFL odds courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook.

In a recent development, it was a modest day at the office for the entire Bears offense in Week 11, but they edged out a 21-13 win over the Saints. For his part, Colston Loveland was targeted just three times. The tight end hauled in all three passes for 29 yards, but did have a thunderous touchdown in the second quarter. That score should serve as the appetizer for a possible eye-popping performance from the Bears star pass catcher in Chicago's upcoming Thanksgiving matchup with the Detroit Lions.

This is the first of two matchups between these NFC North rivals this season, and first place in the division is hanging in the balance during this holiday contest. The Bears are a slight road favorite, and if they want to prove the oddsmakers right, featuring Loveland would go a long way in that endeavor.

Industry observers note that in Week 18 of last season (the last time Loveland played the Lions), the then rookie delivered arguably the best game of his career. He caught 10 of his 13 targets for 91 yards and a touchdown. Those receptions are still his career high. This season, the Lions have been extremely susceptible to tight ends, allowing the most receiving yards (740) and receiving touchdowns (11) to the position in the NFL. They're also giving up the third-most receptions (68) to the position group this season.

This is a tasty matchup that Ben Johnson and firm should look to exploit to come out of Thanksgiving thankful for their ninth win of the season.

Recent findings suggest that gambling angle to note: Colston Loveland's receiving yards prop for Week 12 is 54.5 (-109 to the Over). Loveland is +145 to score a touchdown.

It has been revealed that the vibes surrounding the Rams have been off ever since they kicked off their season opener in Australia. A season marred by injury has seen this once-dubbed "superteam" enter its bye last week at 6-4, on the outside looking in on the playoff picture as the No. 9 seed. As they emerge from the break, however, there is an opportunity in front of them to climb back into the playoff picture, but they'll need a little help.

Industry observers note that first and foremost, they'll need to take care of business during the NFL's first-ever Thanksgiving Eve game where they host the Packers. Green Bay is at the moment clinging to the No. 7 seed in the NFL at 6-4 on the season. A mere win over the Packers on Wednesday would temporarily vault L.A. into the No. 7 seed. However, if they want to hold onto it coming out of Week 12 entirely, they'll need to hold their nose and root for the San Francisco 49ers to defeat the Seattle Seahawks at home.

Industry observers note that that won't be a small feat as Seattle is coming off of its bye and the Niners are coming off an international game in Mexico City. That mentioned, if San Francisco can fend off the defending champions, that'd create the necessary breathing room for the Rams to hold onto their spot in the playoff picture. If the Seahawks win, they'd draw even at 7-4 and retain the tiebreaker thanks to their superior divisional record. It's not an impossible needle to thread, but the Rams will need to get some help over the holiday weekend.

Gambling angle to note: The Rams are -104 to make the playoffs. A Rams-49ers moneyline parlay pays out +159.

Recent findings suggest that A QB controversy has been brewing in the Pacific Northwest, specifically between Sam Darnold and Drew Lock. That talk about a QB controversy has been almost exclusively external, however, as the Seahawks have noted that Darnold -- who has missed the previous two games with rib and quad injuries -- will resume his role as QB1 when healthy. Head coach Mike Macdonald also noted that the team is optimistic that Darnold's return under center will come this week as they emerge from their bye and take on the San Francisco 49ers.

Darnold has been sidelined for essentially four games so far (injured himself on the opening drive of the season opener), so we've seen what the offense looks like with Drew Lock at the helm. He's led Seattle to four wins (3-0 as the starter), while completing 73.1% of his passes and a 125.6 passer rating. By the numbers, Lock has outplayed Darnold from what we've seen so far in 2026, thus bringing up the question of whether or not to keep Lock as the starter.

Industry observers note that again, Darnold will be the guy whenever he's ready to return, so there is no real controversy yet. However, if/when he returns this week, he might be set up for failure, as the 49ers are playing as well as any team in the NFL right now.

If Darnold struggles and the Seahawks lose to the Niners to drop them to 6-5, that chatter to slot in Lock as QB1 will likely reach a fever pitch, particularly with the division and wild card races starting to slip away from them.

According to recent reports, I flagged this in my Cover 32 column for Week 11, but it's worth highlighting yet again. The Pittsburgh Steelers are dangerously close to seeing their season fall out from under them. They were 6-2 entering Week 9, and upon their return to the field, have looked nothing like the club that appeared destined to make the playoffs amid Aaron Rodgers' final season. Pittsburgh has dropped two straight games over the past two weeks, which now has them starting to fall down the wild card standings.

According to recent reports, at 6-4, they're clinging to the No. 7 seed in the conference, which makes Friday's matchup at home against the Denver Broncos as close to a must-win as you'll find in Week 12. The Broncos are a 3-point road favorite in this game, so the oddsmakers are projecting Pittsburgh to fall to 6-5. If they do, they run dangerously close to falling out of the playoff picture entirely.

Temporarily, that'd happen if the New England Patriots go to Los Angeles and beat the Los Angeles Chargers. New England would draw even at 6-5 with Pittsburgh but they own the head-to-head tiebreaker thanks to a Week 2 win. Of course, the Patriots will be without Drake Maye (fractured fibula), but things might be evened out on the QB front as Justin Herbert is right now in concussion protocol coming out of Week 11. That possibly sets up a Tommy DeVito vs. DJ Uiagalelei matchup that is a true coin flip.

It has been revealed that while the Patriots could oust them from a playoff spot for this weekend, the bigger long-term concern is the Houston Texans. They are hosting the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday and are 6.5-point favorites. The double whammy for Pittsburgh would be for them to lose on Friday, see the Patriots beat the Chargers to shoot them down to the No. 8 seed, and then the Texans beat the Ravens to push them to 5-6. That's set up a Week 13 matchup between Pittsburgh and Houston that could very well be the nail in the coffin for their season if they don't turn things around.

Gambling angle to note: A Texans, Patriots, Broncos moneyline parlay is +329.

According to recent reports, it hasn't been the sophomore surge that folks hoped to see from Judkins this season, as the Browns back has struggled to be consistent. His 3.4 yards per carry average is a tick lower than his 3.6 yards per carry over his rookie season and is averaging just 47 rushing yards per game (59.1 yards per game in 14 games as a rookie in 2025). However, Cleveland's "Sunday Night Football" matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders set Judkins up with a true bounce-back opportunity.

The Raiders' run defense has been horrid so far in 2026. Coming into Week 12, Las Vegas is giving up the most rushing yards to running backs in the NFL this season (130.5 yards per game). Their 13 rushing touchdowns allowed are tied for the second-most in the league. The Raiders defense is coming off of a Week 11 loss to the Broncos, where rookie back Jonah Coleman steamrolled them for 111 yards on the ground and three rushing touchdowns.

As he enjoyed his bye week, Judkins was probably licking his chops seeing Coleman post those numbers, knowing full well that he'll get to face them this coming week. Judkins, a 2025 second-round pick, has rushed for at least 100 yards just once in his young career. Well, it wouldn't shock us if he not only notched his second-career game with 100 yards on the ground, but surpassed his 110-yard rushing game from Week 5 last season for a new career-best mark. The Raiders have allowed a 100-yard rusher three times this season already.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that one of the greatest players in Tampa Bay Lightning history may soon be wearing a different jersey. According to Sportsnet, Nikita Kucherov has told the Lightning he won't sign a contract extension and has requested a trade.

According to recent reports, kucherov, a two-time Stanley Cup champion and two-time Hart Trophy winner as league MVP, is one of the best players of his era. The 33-year-old just passed the legendary Steven Stamkos for the all-time franchise lead in points and has shown no signs of slowing down.

Just last season, Kucherov posted 44 goals and 86 assists en route to his second Hart Trophy win. His underlying numbers were even better with a five-on-five goal differential of plus-38 and an expected goals share of 57.0 percent. Only a select few players can drive play from the wing like Kucherov, and that makes him a unicorn of sorts.

Industry observers note that kucherov is in the final year of a contract that pays him $9.5 million per season, and with the salary cap rising rapidly, he's due for a gargantuan raise next summer. It sounds like Kucherov and the Lightning were too far apart on that number, so the superstar winger has shifted his focuse to a change of scenery.

It's crucial to note that Kucherov has limited trade protection in the form of a 10-team trade list, but that should be more than enough for the Lightning to find a suitable trade partner. With that in mind, let's take a look at five teams that would be ideal fits for Kucherov as he prepares for the next chapter of his illustrious career.

According to recent reports, right out of the gate, this is the most natural fit of all the potential landing spots. General manager Kent Hughes has done a superb job of locking down his young core on team-friendly contracts, and as a result, the Canadiens have nearly $30 million in projected cap space for next season. They also have a glaring need in their top two lines, and I'd say the reigning Hart Trophy winner would fill that role quite nicely.

Industry observers note that montreal's moment to strike is now. It's an ascendant team with a great salary cap situtation and assets to spend. It's time to make a splash, and this would be a tsunami. Just imagine Kucherov on a power play unit with Nick Suzuki, Cole Caufield, Lane Hutson and Ivan Demidov. Kucherov would also be coached by former Lightning teammate Martin St. Louis, so a rapport would already exist between player and coach. I expect the Canadiens to do everything in their power to land Kucherov.

We already know the Wild are major-game hunting at forward because they've been heavily linked to former Detroit Red Wings captain Dylan Larkin. If I were advising general manager Bill Guerin -- and I'm certainly not -- I would recommend Minnesota package whatever assets it has offered Detroit and redirect them to Tampa Bay. No, Kucherov is not a center,  and that's the Wild's biggest need.

Industry observers note that however, Kucherov is a rare breed of winger in that he can drive play better than most first-line centers from the wing. Put him on a line with Kirill Kaprizov, and the only time opponents will touch the puck is when they're pulling out of the net.

With Quinn Hughes also on an expiring contract, acquiring Kucherov would be a risky move for the Wild. What if they give up premium assets only to lose Kucherov and Hughes next summer? I don't think fear can dictate Minnesota's decisions. The team has a top-two defenseman in the world on its roster right now, and it has the opportunity to acquire a top-five forward. Worry about next summer when the time comes. Go all in to win the Cup while you have a chance.

It has been revealed that it was no secret that the Hurricanes were in on the Connor Hellebuyck sweepstakes but just missed out. So, if they can't get better at preventing goals, why not get much better at scoring them? Carolina doesn't exactly need any help offensively, but adding Kucherov would go a long way to helping the team repeat as Stanley Cup champions. Besides, Kucherov would provide another level of playmaking and finishing that the Canes don't currently have on their roster.

Carolina has a good chunk of cap space available already, and it wouldn't need to shed much in order to make room for Kucherov. The Canes also have some enticing young players on their roster that might appeal to the Bolts, and they have three first-round picks over the next two drafts. Why not take a shot at landing a superstar winger?

According to recent reports, similar to the Hurricanes, the Mammoth were in the mix to acquire Hellebucyk, and for good reason. The goaltending tandem of Karel Vejmelka and Sebastian Cossa has not been good, so Utah may have to outscore its problems until one of the goalies finds a groove. Offense may be the best defense for the Mammoth -- and if that's the case -- then Kucherov should be in the mix for the Norris Trophy. There is a great young core of forwards in Salt Lake City, and I think Kucherov would be a perfect fit alongside Logan Cooley, who is emerging as a franchise center.

In a recent development, utah also has plenty of draft capital with which to work, and it's projected for just over $25 million in salary cap space next season. The Mammoth don't have any major pending free agents on their cap sheet, so they're a suitor capable of signing Kucherov to a long-term extension.

Industry observers note that allow me to get a little bold on the fifth and final destination. The Stars have already failed to sign 27-year-old winger Jason Robertson to a long-term extension once. The two sides agreed to a one-year deal worth $12 million prior to the season, but Robertson's future with the team is still very much in doubt. What if Dallas and Tampa Bay executed a true "hockey trade" -- one player for one player?

In a recent development, dallas would get the better player in Kucherov, but there are no guarantees regarding an extension. The Stars are in win-now mode, and Kucherov could help them get over the Cup hump immediately. Tampa Bay would get a younger player in Robertson, and although he doesn't have the elite playmaking ability of Kucherov, he's still an exceptionally talented scorer. Perhaps the Bolts could get him to join the team's core and sign a multi-year contract. This deal could work for both sides.

PSV Eindhoven endured a frustrating night in the Champions League as their defensive frailties were exposed in a 2-1 defeat by Club Brugge.

PSV started full of attacking intent and should have taken an early lead when Ivan Perisic put Sergiño Dest clean through on goal, but the defender’s shot was too close to goalkeeper Yann Sommer.

Instead it was the visitors who took the lead with their first real attack when Nicolo Tresoldi headed in a teasing cross from Joaquin Seys.

According to recent reports, PSV equalised early in the second half as an outstanding pass by Sven Mijnans into the path Lutsharel Geertruida allowed the defender to charge to the byline. His pullback found its way to Kodai Sano, whose shot took a deflection off Seys into the net.

But five minutes later PSV were caught out as another razor-sharp pass by Seys released Carlos Forbs in space to net the winner.

The home side refused to give up, but were unable to find a way past Sommer in the closing stages as the Belgian side closed out the win.

Team captain Mauro Junior admitted that PSV had been undone by shortcomings at the back. “We had a lot of opportunities in the first half but we didn’t score,” he told Ziggo Sport.

It has been revealed that “We want to attack and score goals, but we weren’ well organised today in defence. We need to keep our heads up and look forward to the next game.”.

The result leaves PSV in 24th place, just above the elimination line, ahead of their next match away to Real Madrid on November 24, with four points from their opening four matches.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • When I think about Thanksgiving, I think about going to my grandparents' house growing up.
  • Around midnight — sometimes later — we'd arrive at my grandparents' doorstep, weary but happy.
  • And then there was Thanksgiving Day, which meant football.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When I think about Thanksgiving, I think about going to my grandparents' house growing up. We'd leave immediately after my dad got off work on Wednesday and drive from my hometown in rural Virginia to my mom's parents in New Jersey. A quick stop at the McDonald's was the only time we'd leave our route. We'd drive extra miles to avoid traffic. I'd try, often unsuccessfully, to fight off sleep on the drive up.

Around midnight — sometimes later — we'd arrive at my grandparents' doorstep, weary but happy. They'd always greet us with smiling faces, no matter the hour.

And then there was Thanksgiving Day, which meant football. My grandpa, a die-hard Giants fan, would lead our collective yelling at the TV, hoping the Cowboys would lose, and we'd pity-root for the Lions, who seemingly never won.

The results fade, but what I remember is my family being together. It wasn't perfect. It got harder as my grandparents got older. We'd laugh, we'd cheer, we'd wish it could last forever.

It's been several years since then, but I still remember my grandparents waving us goodbye, my grandpa good-heartedly reminding my dad to go south, not north, on the turnpike. It felt like just minutes earlier, they had been standing in that doorway welcoming us in. It always went too fast.

It has been revealed that so ahead of our six lessons, let me give you a non-football one: Try to cherish this week. If you can do it with family, great. If you can do it with friends, great. If all you can do is call or text, great. It doesn't have to be perfect. Whether you watch every football game this week or none at all, I hope you're surrounded by people you love.

Coach of the Year has become so misconstrued, and not just in the NFL. Every individual player award honors the best player, but for some reason Coach of the Year honors the coach whose team exceeds expectations most.

So, once again, Kyle Shanahan's magnificent job will likely go unrewarded, simply because he's done too good a job for too long. An early congratulations to either John Harbaugh or Todd Monken for winning. They've done magnificent jobs.

But Kyle Shanahan is the best coach in the NFL this season. The 49ers just dismantled the Vikings to move to 9-1. They have won games in Australia and Mexico and Seattle and Dallas, all places with their own unique challenges. They have won games using wide receivers they never imagined having to count on.

Recent findings suggest that thought you saw the best of Brock Purdy? Think again. I've written at length about why Purdy deserves MVP and is much more than just a product of the Shanahan system, but there's no doubt Shanahan has raised his game immensely. This offense is so well-constructed, so prepared for each and every task each and every week and so connected.

According to recent reports, the Vikings love to blitz. Purdy shredded them with quick passes: 12-for-13 for 161 yards and two touchdowns on throws released in 2.5 seconds or faster. Minnesota entered the night leading the NFL in sack rate and pressure rate. It managed just one sack and a 29% pressure rate, both season lows.

This is nothing fresh, by the way.

Oh yeah, and Shanahan also made the excellent hire of defensive coordinator Raheem Morris, who has helped turn this defense from quite poor to elite.

In a recent development, it's silly that we'll look back and likely see someone else win Coach of the Year. Shanahan has never won the award, by the way, even though he's been the best or among the best in the profession for nearly a decade. Andy Reid, who's fourth all-time in wins, has won it once, back in 2002 with the Eagles. Sean McVay has won it once since becoming a head coach in 2017. Kevin Stefanski, a perfectly solid coach but nothing more, has won it twice.

Again, even if he doesn't win "Coach of the Year," Shanahan is very much the defining coach of this year. He'd gladly take a Lombardi Trophy over any individual award, anyway.

One day after Brian Flores' normally excellent defense was shredded, one of his disciplines had his best performance yet. Commanders defensive coordinator Daronte Jones and his unit were terrific in a 22-20 upset win over the Bengals.

Jones, like Flores, brings extra pressure, substantial time. Washington is third in blitz rate this year. Joe Burrow has destroyed blitzes all year, but on Monday night, not so much.

According to recent reports, jones was without his best cornerback, Amik Robertson, but refused to back down. His corners played physically, aggressively and well. The safeties followed in kind. And while Cincinnati's running game has never been a strength, Washington turned it into a decided weakness. The Bengals' 14% rushing success rate was the worst by any team in any game this year.

Jones has this defense moving in the right direction, too. In November, the Commanders rank 15th in defensive EPA per play; they were 23rd before that. They've done a good job stopping the run and limiting explosives, largely because they have the third-lowest missed tackle rate in the league. Washington hasn't allowed more than 23 points in a game since Week 5.

There will be big-picture coaching questions in Washington if the team doesn't make the playoffs, but Jones has done solid work under the radar.

According to recent reports, I wrote about this in our Week 11 overreactions, but the Steelers are once again a team with a winning record and little chance of winning a playoff game. Here, though, let's talk about the style.

Aaron Rodgers is now completing 21.6% of his passes thrown 20+ yards downfield. While he is throwing way more of them this year — only Jordan Love has more than Rodgers' 51 attempts — they're mostly performative "See? I'll still take shots downfield" throws that are low-percentage floaters. Only Cam Ward and recently released Daniel Jones have a lower completion rate on these throws.

The run game can be quite good. In fact, the Steelers are second in rushing EPA per play this year at 0.06. Earlier in the season, it seemed they finally had one truly sterling offensive aspect. This made them different.

Industry observers note that but when the run game isn't going well, as has been the case the last two weeks, Pittsburgh has nothing else. The Steelers are 4-0 when their EPA per rush is above their overall season mark and 2-4 when it is below it. Pittsburgh was at -0.19, second-worst of the season, in the Week 11 loss to the Eagles.

The Steelers have been the same as they've been during this playoff win drought: poor quarterbacking, good-not-great defense.

Industry observers note that K. Pickett, M. Rudolph, M. Trubisky.

Just a dull, stuck-going-nowhere team archetype and a franchise that seems fine with it.

The Chiefs' three-game winning streak has coincided with a soft schedule. There's not a ton to take away from it in terms of Kansas City's standing in the championship-contending pecking order.

Recent findings suggest that but on an individual level, Emmett Johnson is a beast. In his two starts with Kenneth Walker III out, Johnson has 134 yards from scrimmage and three touchdowns.

Emmett Johnson has now recorded back to back 100 yard rushing games since taking over for Kenneth Walker.23 CAR, 105 RUSH YDS, 1 TD, 4 REC, 38 REC YDS vs Cardinals.Johnson's OROY chances have skyrocketed over the last two weeks. https://t.co/dt5FdKVwLi pic.twitter.com/tNep8zsuxb.

In a recent development, johnson right now leads all running backs in 7.0 yards per touch (min. 50 touches). He also leads all running backs in tackle avoidance rate (36.8), which is also first and slightly higher than tackle-avoiding machine Walker III.

It has been revealed that johnson has a true three-down skill set. Only 11.3% of his rushes go for 0 or negative yards, the fourth-lowest rate among all running backs with at least 50 touches, and he has turned several potential losses into gains.

Industry observers note that walker is a stud. He'll be the feature back when he returns from his groin injury. But Johnson has proved he not only deserves a legit complementary role down the stretch and beyond, but with his pass-catching acumen, he can actually be a weapon, too.

The Colts got thumped 26-3 by the Texans on Thursday, and that somehow wasn't the worst aspect of their week. Not even close.

One day after that, Indianapolis released Daniel Jones, and shortly after that, reports surfaced that at the trade deadline, the Colts had turned down the Ravens' offer of a fourth-and fifth-round pick for Jones (the fifth would be returned if Baltimore made the playoffs). Now, they get nothing for Jones and will carry a $35.2 million dead cap hit in 2027.

In a recent development, if interim GM Ed Dodds wasn't already filling in for a fired GM (Chris Ballard), this would be a fireable offense. Maybe it is, anyway. The Colts sold away many of their franchise pillars but stopped at Daniel Jones?

According to various reports, the Colts turned away multiple suitors for Jones, including Baltimore's potentially lucrative one; multiple suitors for Jonathan Taylor, who fetched offers for a second-round pick plus more; at least one offer that included a fourth-round pick for veteran defensive tackle Grover Stewart, who's 33 and in a contract year.

I gave the Colts a D+ in my trade deadline grades and, upon first reflection, thought I might have been a little harsh. Indianapolis did get decent draft capital back for the moves it did make. But now, I think that mark might be generous. Every meaningless hard hit Taylor takes, and every meaningless double-team Stewart takes on, is just that. Meaningless.

The Colts have very little young, cost-controlled talent. They don't have their first-round pick in 2027. They will have a new GM and, likely, a new coach. They are arguably the worst team in the NFL in 2026. They will be in the running for worst team in the NFL in 2027 and potentially 2028. They just turned down draft capital for a player they didn't even want. If there were a class in mismanaging an enterprise worth billions of dollars, the Colts' front office could do a great job teaching it.

It has been revealed that if it feels like there's been a little bit of a midseason lull, it's because there has been. In November, there's been a ton of blowouts — seven games decided by 15+ every week from Week 8-10, and then a lot of byes and semi-competitive games in Week 11.

But the league is cranking it up a notch this coming week.

Industry observers note that the Bears have won five straight, but their last two are over the lowly Buccaneers and Saints, with a bye in between. The Lions have won six straight, but the last three are over the Dolphins, the Patriots (mostly without Drake Maye) and the Buccaneers. I'm a huge believer in "you can only beat who's on your schedule." But in terms of learning about these teams, the past few weeks haven't been very helpful.

That all changes this week. On Thanksgiving, the 8-2 Lions host the 8-2 Bears (on CBS and streaming on Paramount+, by the way!), which should be an absolute banger.

This is far from the only example. Get your nap in early, because later that night, Chiefs at Bills is a can't-miss. Buffalo has seemed almost bored — and certainly hasn't been very sharp — in wins over the Ravens, Carson Wentz-led Vikings, Jets and Dolphins. But they'll absolutely be locked in against their bitter rival. The Chiefs, meanwhile, have cruised past the Jets, Falcons and Saints after a tough loss to the Broncos. We have questions about Josh Allen's turnovers, Patrick Mahomes' deep-passing renaissance — is it real or fake? — and much more.

Arsenal teach Chelsea a lesson in how to be champions

📅 06 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 33 min read (6617 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~33 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • This is how champions are supposed to play and, although the Arsenal home support have not seen a team defend their place at the apex of English league football for two decades, they knew it when they saw it.
  • The chase was on for Mikel Arteta’s team within two minutes when Morgan Rogers, the man who might have moved to Arsenal this summer, put his fresh club Chelsea in the lead.
  • According to recent reports, others might have crumbled.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This is how champions are supposed to play and, although the Arsenal home support have not seen a team defend their place at the apex of English league football for two decades, they knew it when they saw it.

The chase was on for Mikel Arteta’s team within two minutes when Morgan Rogers, the man who might have moved to Arsenal this summer, put his fresh club Chelsea in the lead. So unfolded a thrilling 100 minutes of Premier League competition. Arsenal were the better team in terms of ambition and attack even if one could not discount Chelsea until the very last moment.

According to recent reports, others might have crumbled. That Chelsea did not will give Xabi Alonso hope for a team that did not feature the injured Moisés Caicedo and is now without the departed Enzo Fernández. Yet he will also recognise that his childhood friend from San Sebastián in the other dugout has created a side that treated the game, and their place in it, with an urgency that looks different. The first two minutes might have been ragged for Arsenal but after that they did not let the game happen to them.

Morgan Rogers fires Chelsea in front inside TWO minutes! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/ca8cqnT2Wm.

Industry observers note that instead, Arteta’s players drove this contest, and the sequence of chances that came and went was dizzying at times. Their best players scored the two goals. First Kai Havertz, who now has three in four games this season, and then the captain Martin Ødegaard who dispatched what would be the winner.

"A spear through the heart of Chelsea!" Martin Odegaard puts Arsenal in front at the Emirates 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5deEQykjck.

Ødegaard looked like the veteran of a title-winning season, and a deep run in the World Cup – an accomplished, shrewd performer in a midfield that was fought over ferociously all afternoon.

Sources indicate that as for the game’s defining moment – it would be hard to overlook the feint from Havertz for the winning goal. It deceived the Chelsea players around him and created the channel for Christos Tzolis’s cross to reach Ødegaard. His goal was a close copy, in style and personnel, of the one he scored against Manchester City in the Community Shield but it was crowned by Havertz’s bluff. He shaped to take the ball and let it run under his foot at the last moment.

This was Chelsea’s first defeat in three – leaving only Arsenal and City with nine points from their first three games – although the seven goals conceded is the standout. For all the jet fuel in their attack they keep conceding. This was a much more exacting test than Fulham and Brighton previously, but even so. Alonso has introduced his preferred back three, often a back five, and it is a work in progress.

Arsenal have set the standard in that regard and they were uncompromising again. They did not replicate the errors that led to the Rogers goal and they pushed the limits at all times. Gabriel Magalhães kicked Emi Martínez in the head competing for a ball in the Chelsea area. Myles Lewis-Skelly went after João Pedro. Ben White and Roméo Lavia saw things differently in the first half. This Arsenal team does not shy away from those confrontations in the way their predecessors often did.

It has been revealed that in fact, it was notable just how furiously Rogers reacted to Declan Rice when the two England team-mates converged as the Chelsea man charged off to join a late counter-attack. The bad feeling lingered even after the game when Rogers seemed unwilling to forgive. Rice had applied the minimum contact and the maximum cynicism to stop Rogers while the attention of referee Chris Kavanagh was elsewhere.

"He's FUMING Morgan Rogers!" 😳 pic.twitter.com/FciivEedvh.

Industry observers note that all that ringcraft was one thing, but it should be said that Arsenal were excellent in setting an attacking tempo that will be hell for any team to live with – especially at the Emirates. Havertz is now Arteta’s centre-forward of choice in the absence of a big summer acquisition. Viktor Gyökeres made a late substitute’s appearance – his first minutes of the season. The hierarchy is clear: last season’s great goalscoring hope is now back-up.

It has been revealed that “Exceptional” was how Arteta described his team’s response to the early Rogers goal. They had twice failed to clear the ball in their own area when first Maxence Lacroix and then Jorrel Hato created the chance. Rogers’s right foot half-volley was not struck on the full, but it was placed perfectly inside the post with the necessary bounce and skip to mean David Raya never got behind it.

Arteta’s squad runs deep enough that in the closing stages he could relieve his midfield with two Spanish World Cup-winning substitutes – Martín Zubimendi and Mikel Merino. Then there was Noni Madueke on for Bukayo Saka, understudy and first-choice for club and country. This was not Saka’s day in the way it has been in the past, although a very promising shot of his was stopped by Martinez in the first half.

In the pounding that Chelsea took after they went into the lead, Riccardo Calafiori had an equaliser within minutes that was disallowed by VAR on an offside call. The left-back was the third in sequence to try to force the ball over the line from a Rice free-kick. Calafiori was successful, but the second of his team-mates to try, Ezri Konsa, had been offside when he connected.

It has been revealed that for the equaliser it was Havertz, accelerating cautiously at first and then full-on with his left foot from the right-side. Ødegaard was well-placed to prevent Lacroix getting close but in truth the challenge never had the force required. Havertz’s shot was not totally convincing but then neither was Martinez’s attempt to save it – every bit as uncertain as Raya for the Chelsea goal.

A precise finish from Kai Havertz and Arsenal are level! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/DqL1MEX4zN.

In a recent development, chelsea had profited from the quick ball out to their right where Calafiori was often out of position in the left-back slot and Pedro Neto could cut in on his left foot. That seemed to be the sacrifice that Arteta was prepared to make in keeping the hammer on Chelsea. If Neto had not struck the post in one such escape in time added on at the end of the first half it might have been different.

Ødegaard struck what would be the winner early in the first half, and although Chelsea fizzed enough in the later stages it always felt as though it was Arsenal’s game. Raya came into his own in the 89th minute when Estêvão, a substitute, cut in from the right and hit a fierce shot that the goalkeeper pushed over. It was close in some ways – and in others not at all.

Recent findings suggest that “It hurts. It hurts because a defeat has to hurt. It has been a very intense game with different moments for everything. We had chances to equalise. In the first half as well a couple of chances. Never happy if you lose.

“After we scored, there were 15-20 minutes where we had to defend too much and we were struggling a bit to get control. We then had better spells with the ball. Overall, it was a very tight, very intense game. We could do better with the second goal to conceded too early. The guys gave everything, tried everything. It has to hurt.

It has been revealed that “It is about preparing the best possible way to compete the best possible way. You need to control the overloads on the right side. It is part of the game to have these actions. We continue. It is game three and this is going to be a long, long ride.”.

"That's not sustainable" Daniel Sturridge reflects Chelsea's performance after the 2-1 defeat to Arsenal 💭 pic.twitter.com/3EMx88QLA0.

"He's not the goalkeeper that won the World Cup" 🏆Jamie Carragher says Emi Martinez is not as quick or sharp as he once was 🧤 pic.twitter.com/SOp4XhoYIr.

Sources indicate that “I think the worrying thing for everybody else already is that [William] Saliba, who is genuinely world-class arguably, probably the best centre-back in world football, has not played a minute of football so far this season. It is a relationship that Arteta has previously described as “deeper than just a friendship”. It started with skateboards and sand, as they made the daily journey to the beach to play tennis and football, and continued into their adult lives. When Alonso was playing for Liverpool and Arteta for Everton, there was a time when they both had flats on the fourth floor of the same building in the Albert Dock.

Industry observers note that it is extraordinary that these two individuals – born just a few months apart – now find themselves in positions of such significance in English football. But it is not a coincidence. Throughout their lives, they have driven each other forward.

“This kid, he was maybe even crazier than me about football,” Alonso once remarked of Arteta and their shared childhood. “He was a little bit younger than me and my friends – just a few months maybe. But you know how you always push your ‘little friends’ at that age? Well, we tried, but he was a competitive monster.”.

Recent findings suggest that A personal opinion that no one asked for: Arsenal should have signed Joao Pedro last summer, when the Brazilian joined Chelsea for £60m. Arsenal bought Viktor Gyokeres instead, in a deal that could ultimately be more expensive, and there is no doubt which forward offers more to their team. Joao Pedro always seemed to cause problems for Arsenal’s defence when he played against them during his time at Brighton, and he has a flexibility and versatility that would have been perfect for Arteta’s system. Arsenal had twice explored the possibility of signing him over the years. It is surely a source of regret that they never became serious about it. Recent findings suggest that mikel Arteta insists Arsenal are “better equipped” for success this season, despite falling short in their attempts to add a top-class attacker. Arsenal have allowed four forward players to leave this summer and brought in one, Greece winger Christos Tzolis.

The departures of Gabriel Martinelli, Leandro Trossard, Gabriel Jesus and Ethan Nwaneri (on loan) have raised concerns among supporters that the champions lack firepower. Moves for Morgan Rogers, Vinicius Junior and Julian Alvarez did not come to fruition. Arteta, though, feels Arsenal are stronger now than at the end of last season following a summer in which they added midfielder Bruno Guimarães and defender Ezri Konsa.

According to recent reports, “We are better equipped,” said Arteta, who faces Rogers and close friend Xabi Alonso. “We have more players available than the start of last season. We have increased the quality and we have increased the leadership, which is very important.”.

Asked specifically about the attack, he added: “Yeah, but that’s another question. We have to prove in that particular position whether we are better or not. Let’s see. We need to play. I don’t like to make assumptions.

“It’s not just the responsibility of those players, it’s the team and the dynamic. We have multiple options to play there with different profiles. It’s human nature. When you talk to people and you ask: ‘Ok, what is on your bucket list?’ Sometimes we forget the reverse bucket list, which are the things you already have that are incredible. It’s very important to value what we have, what we have created together. The ambition is great, but [don’t] lose perspective to what we already have which is amazing.”.

Two sides with 100% records meet in a London derby in north London as defending champions Arsenal host Chelsea at the Emirates. Arsenal have wins over Coventry and Aston Villa to their name whilst Chelsea have beaten Fulham and Brighton.

Arsenal could make it three wins from three to start the season, a feat they have only achieved once in the last 21 seasons. They have lost just one of their last 29 Premier League London derbies. Mikel Arteta comes up against his childhood friend Xabi Alonso today.

Industry observers note that “Really happy for him [Alonso],” Arteta mentioned. “It is incredible because obviously we have the history we have together, the same with Andoni [Iraola]. To be facing each other at such a level and with the responsibility we have managing some of the top clubs in the country is a really beautiful thing to experience. Now it will be tougher to meet because of the schedule we both have but that friendship will go for many years. We shared some great moments but now it is the competition and when you face each other, you know what happens.”.

Recent findings suggest that chelsea were involved in late drama on transfer deadline day. They were on the verge of signing midfielder Lamine Camara from Monaco only to see that deal fall through at the last minute. After being linked with a move away throughout the summer, Chelsea did in the end sell Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City for a joint Premier League transfer record fee of £125m.

“In football, many things happen and you need to be prepared for everything,” Chelsea boss Alonso remarked. “With Enzo, we have had conversations, but always with respect for what he has done for the club. It has been great, we are thankful, but it is time to move forward. We take all the decisions together. We are responsible for them, we work together with every decision, significant and small.

It has been revealed that “We knew that, ultimately, the last goal is to have the best for the team, the best for the squad, the best for daily work here. We want to build a good spirit, a good team, and we have always taken decisions thinking we want to reach that. We have the squad we have. We have a lot of major personalities, players with a lot of quality in all the different positions, different lines and now we are ready to go.”.

Arsenal won this fixture 2-1 last season, with William Saliba and Jurrien Timber earning Mikel Arteta’s side three points on their way to the title. Arsenal are unbeaten in their last nine Premier League matches against Chelsea.
