#119902. Kyrie Irving to the Jazz? Why Utah's reported interest in the star Mavericks guard makes no sense

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1439 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

Kyrie Irving to the Jazz? Why Utah's reported interest in the star Mavericks guard makes no sense

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1439 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • They will consider almost any path to improving their rosters, no matter how obscure or unexpected.
  • In a recent development, on Thursday, one such rumor arrived as SNY's Ian Begley reported that the Utah Jazz have given Kyrie Irving "internal consideration as a potential trade candidate." Now, this is common.
  • So, let's consider this rumor in earnest.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

NBA teams are remarkably diligent. They will consider almost any path to improving their rosters, no matter how obscure or unexpected. Still, every now and then, a truly bizarre nugget hits the rumor mill and forces us to consider what exactly a team is thinking.

In a recent development, on Thursday, one such rumor arrived as SNY's Ian Begley reported that the Utah Jazz have given Kyrie Irving "internal consideration as a potential trade candidate." Now, this is common. Teams will do due diligence on a wide variety of players leading up to transaction periods in order to make sure they've covered their bases, and Begley gives no indication that there have even been talks between the Jazz and the Dallas Mavericks. Still, as he notes, "you're not gonna spend a lot of time on a player if you don't have any interest in him, so the idea of Utah spending some time internally on Kyrie Irving was interesting.".

So, let's consider this rumor in earnest. The Jazz entered this season with playoff expectations after four straight years in the lottery. They are 3-13 due to a combination of injuries, players adjusting to a new roster and simply poor performance. Utah has shown a willingness to trade for players outside of its perceived timeline before. The Jazz looked at then-33-year-old Jrue Holiday early in their rebuild in 2023, for instance, but backed off when Holiday's camp reportedly made it clear he would not be interested in extending.

Irving, still a star-caliber scorer, has the Mavericks at 8-7 through 15 games. He's averaging over 22 points on roughly his standard efficiency for a Dallas team with pretty limited shooting around him. We can't say at this stage whether or not the Mavericks are willing to trade him. The notion that they might depends on the team's asset deficit (Dallas does not control its own first-round pick again until 2031) and the 15-year age gap between Irving and franchise player Cooper Flagg, but Dallas could easily elect to simply build off this early success.

In a recent development, if they do take the long view and consider trade offers, Irving could absolutely help a team trying to win right now. Plenty of teams potentially looking for individual shot-creation, like the Detroit Pistons, Houston Rockets and Miami Heat, could be planning pursuits of the future Hall of Famer.

The question here is why the Jazz, specifically, would be interested in Irving, because on paper, there is perhaps not a single, high-profile player who makes less sense for this roster than he does. Utah's young core revolves around three perimeter players: Keyonte George, Darryn Peterson and Ace Bailey. The Jazz are so strong on that front that Bailey came off the bench to start the season, and it's unclear how exactly they strategy to handle their starting five when Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr. return from injuries. If Utah isn't comfortable with Jackson playing center full time, and the Memphis Grizzlies certainly weren't, then one of those five players either needs to get traded or come off the bench.

Adding Irving to this logjam doesn't make sense. Neither does trading one of those players for Irving. George is 23. Bailey is 20. Peterson is 19. Teams that are 10 games below .500 simply don't trade foundational pieces for players a decade or more their senior. They gave up three first-round picks for Jackson largely to improve their defense, and now that Walker Kessler plays for the Los Angeles Lakers, his presence matters more than ever.

According to recent reports, markkanen is the obvious trade candidate of the group, but he's still five years younger than Irving and plays a less saturated position. If Utah viewed Markkanen's max contract as a negative it needed to escape, that would be one thing, but there's just no evidence at this stage that this is the case. They have rebuffed trade interest in Markkanen at every turn. If Dallas were willing to put substantial draft equity on the table to cover the age and positional gaps here, there could perhaps be a conversation, but Dallas isn't in a position to do so.

It has been revealed that there's some merit to the idea that Utah might eventually want to shake up its backcourt. There were rumors during the draft process that Peterson's representatives were skeptical of Utah as a landing spot because they also represent George and felt that two score-first guards would clash. Even if the Jazz were prepared to split them up less than 20 games into Peterson's career, Irving himself has typically fared far better when he has been paired with a high-level passer. He won his championship with LeBron James. He's thriving next to Cooper Flagg now. His best trait is, and always has been, his scoring.

Recent findings suggest that and then, of course, there is the history shared between Irving and Utah's top executive. The CEO of the Jazz is Danny Ainge, who once traded for Irving when he ran the Boston Celtics. Before his second season in Boston, Irving publicly shared plans to re-sign with the Celtics as a free agent in 2019. When the time came, he instead joined the Brooklyn Nets, a divisional opponent. This is the NBA. If LeBron James can reunite with Dan Gilbert, any player-executive reunion is theoretically possible. Nonetheless, Ainge and Irving would seemingly be among the unlikeliest pairings in all of basketball. Put all of this together and this is a puzzling rumor to say the least.

Sometimes a rumor notes more about a team's big-picture looks than it does a specific target. For a variety of reasons, some of which we've covered, it seems exceedingly unlikely that the Jazz are going to trade for Irving. However, they've invested the time in considering it, as Begley noted. That means something, even if it doesn't mean a trade is coming.

According to recent reports, the simplest read on this is that Utah is concerned enough about its short-term prospects that it is considering investing in win-now help despite its 3-13 start. That, in itself, makes sense. The Jazz don't control their own first-round pick this season. They have no incentive to lose, and while making the postseason despite starting the season 10 games under .500 is improbable, it just happened a year ago when the 4-14 Charlotte Hornets recovered swiftly enough to reach the Play-In Tournament. The Jazz are 5.5 games out of the No. 10 seed in the Western Conference right now. If they get healthy in time and make the right addition, perhaps they could still make a real run at it.

It has been revealed that skepticism about the George-Peterson fit, for now, should be on the back burner. Though the two fared far better early on when they played separately, both, at least for now, have better net ratings and true shooting percentages in the minutes they've shared than the minutes they haven't. George's usage skyrockets when he plays without Peterson, but that's to be expected with Markkanen and Jackson out.

It has been revealed that there may have been concern early in the season, and that might have been when Irving crossed Utah's mind. There may still be concerns down the line when the Jazz have had a longer sample size to evaluate the pairing with the rest of their roster. For now, though, it's simply too early to consider splitting up such a talented tandem, especially right as the team has actually started winning some games.

However, ball-handling behind them is a valid concern. Utah declined its fourth-year option on backup point guard and former first-round pick Isaiah Collier, and the offense has been 6.5 points per 100 possessions worse with him on the floor this season. Adding a veteran backup point guard, if only to ease Peterson's burden during the minutes George rests, would be sensible. Irving is obviously no backup, but as perhaps the most notable point guard theoretically on the market, it makes sense that the Jazz would at least broach the concept internally.

It has been revealed that ainge hasn't earned the nickname "Trader Danny" for nothing. His teams are almost always at the center of the trade market, and as last year's Jackson deal proved, he's as capable of a stunner as he's ever been. Irving would certainly qualify as one. We shouldn't expect it. It wouldn't really make sense based on what we know now. But in the post-Luka Dončić trade NBA, it would be hard to dismiss basically any rumor involving a player of this stature.

#119901. Breaking: Why a long-term mega deal for Tarik Skubal isn't actually all that risky

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1271 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Why a long-term mega deal for Tarik Skubal isn't actually all that risky

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1271 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The big prize of this free agent class, ace lefty and two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal, has landed with the Mets on a nine-year, $450 million deal.
  • The knee-jerk reaction to a contract of this size in many corners will be that he won't possibly be "worth" that much and that such a deal would be a huge "risk" to the signing team.
  • Sources indicate that let's stop right there.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The big prize of this free agent class, ace lefty and two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal, has landed with the Mets on a nine-year, $450 million deal.

The knee-jerk reaction to a contract of this size in many corners will be that he won't possibly be "worth" that much and that such a deal would be a huge "risk" to the signing team.

Sources indicate that let's stop right there. I don't think it's all that risky. There's risk for the team on every contract, especially pitchers, of course, but in Skubal, the Mets are getting a surefire ace for nearly a decade.

Let's examine some of the reasons why such an enormous deal isn't actually that dangerous.

It has been revealed that since returning from surgery in 2023, Skubal has been absurdly good. Across his ages 26-29 seasons, he's made 103 starts and has gone 50-20 with a 2.47 ERA (169 ERA+), 0.92 WHIP and 757 strikeouts in 626 ⅓ innings. He's only walked 109, or 1.6 per nine innings. He rarely gets hit hard, he rarely gives up many runs, he strikes out a high number of hitters and rarely walks any. Simply, he's been good at everything.

The recent track record here states this is the best pitcher in baseball, at least in the long view (we could argue Paul Skenes was better in 2025 and Jacob Misiorowski was better in 2026, to name two examples, but if we looked at 2023-present, it isn't all that close).

Sources indicate that there isn't a dropoff in the postseason, either. In eight playoff starts, Skubal has a 2.13 ERA, 0.79 WHIP and 70 strikeouts against nine unintentional walks in 50 ⅔ innings.

According to recent reports, he's stellar. Pretty much all the time.

Also, the career workload isn't anything to be concerned about. Skubal heads to his age-30 season now with only 925 ⅓ innings in the regular season. Even counting the playoffs doesn't get Skubal to 1,000 innings at the big-league level. Let's go back to Skenes. He's only 24 years old and already has 495 career innings. Another ace? Justin Verlander had 1,553 ⅔ career innings through his age-29 season.

There just isn't a ton of tread on these Skubal tires.

We'll hear plenty of consternation about Skubal being 30 years old next season as it relates to signing a long-term deal. We'll also hear people say a deal is risky due to his injury history. He had Tommy John surgery in college, flexor tendon surgery in 2022 and arthroscopic surgery (a new procedure using a Nanoscope) in 2026.

The simple matter is that pretty much every pitcher nowadays has had some sort of surgery on his arm, notably the elbow, and we've seen pitchers time and again bounce back after elbow surgery to perform at a high level.

Recent findings suggest that skubal just did it. He only missed roughly six weeks after his procedure this past season. He came back to make 19 starts after the surgery and posted a 2.73 ERA with 141 strikeouts in 115 ⅓ innings.

In a recent development, I mentioned Verlander above. Skubal is a multi-time Cy Young winner, so it's acceptable to look at some of the best pitchers in baseball and how they aged into their late-30s in recent memory.

Sources indicate that again, Skubal will be in his age-30 season in 2027. His nine-year deal means it'll run through his age-38 season.

For those so worried about the long-term finances of the Cohen family, are you sure you're really worried that Skubal won't be productive through five, six or even all nine years of that deal? Given his track record, talent, pitching arsenal, relatively low workload given his age and how well some of the best pitchers have fared through their mid-30s, he actually seems like a great bet.

Industry observers note that A decade ago, the common talking point was that long and huge deals for pitchers never age well. That isn't actually the case, for the most part. Here are some of the biggest pitcher contracts of all time and how they unfolded (or are unfolding).

Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Dodgers, 12 years, $325 million -- He came over from Japan for his age-25 season, so this one was a different animal. Still, it sure doesn't seem like it'll be a bad deal, does it?

In a recent development, gerrit Cole, Yankees, 9 years, $324 million -- Through six years of the deal, Cole has missed a chunk of time due to Tommy John surgery. He's also won a Cy Young, finished top four in Cy Young voting three times, been worth 22.4 WAR and was the ace of an American League pennant winner.

Stephen Strasburg, Nationals, 7 years, $245 million -- Here's the bust. Strasburg was never healthy again after the 2019 World Series title run. Still, the Nationals wouldn't have that title without him.

It has been revealed that justin Verlander, Tigers, 10 years, $219.5 million -- This was the deal that ran from 2010-19. During this deal, Verlander won two Cy Youngs (one in the second year of the deal, one in the final year), a World Series, three pennants, 160 games and led the league in pitcher WAR three times.

Max Fried, Yankees, 8 years, $218 million -- It's only been two years, but Fried is 24-10 with a 2.83 ERA and finished fourth in AL Cy Young voting in his first year.

Industry observers note that david Price, Red Sox, 7 years, $217 million -- He won a World Series in the third year of the contract. Overall, he was 53-26 with a 3.78 ERA (118 ERA+) through the course of the deal.

Corbin Burnes, Diamondbacks, 6 years, $210 million -- Burnes had his first year of the deal interrupted by Tommy John surgery. He had a 2.66 ERA through 11 starts prior to the injury. The jury's still out, but he heads to his age-32 season fully recovered now.

Sources indicate that zack Greinke, 6 years, $206.5 million -- Over the course of this deal, Greinke was 77-39 with a 3.55 ERA (125 ERA+) and 19.9 WAR. He had a fourth-place Cy Young finish in there.

CC Sabathia, 9 years, $202 million -- The Yankees won the World Series in Sabathia's first year there and he started the deal with three straight top-four Cy Young finishes. Overall, during this deal, he was 120-73 with 27.1 WAR and had five straight 200-plus inning seasons.

Industry observers note that max Scherzer, 7 years, $191.4 million -- During this contract, Scherzer won two Cy Youngs, a World Series title and 99 games with a 2.75 ERA. He posted 41.8 WAR. In the seven years on this deal, Scherzer finished in the top five in Cy Young voting six times, with 2020 being the outlier.

We can close with this. Some people might not care for such a measure, particularly the salary cap crowd who will be worried about the owners paying too much. Regardless, let's stick with the general belief that each individual WAR (1.0 WAR) is worth a bit over $8 million per season.

According to recent reports, by this measure, Skubal was worth $48.4 million in 2024, $53.7 million in 2025 and $41.7 million last season. Putting aside how much less money he actually made than what he was doing on the field, and knowing everything laid out above, I'll ask a simple question:.

Are you sure a 9-year, $450 million deal for this guy is a "risk?".

I think we could argue that it'll be a bargain.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • We're just over one month into the season, and the Pittsburgh Penguins are three games below .500 and 15th in the Eastern Conference.
  • On the heels of a resurgence in 2025-26, the Penguins haven't quite been able to recapture that magic yet, and there's a good chance Father Time has something to do with that.
  • Recent findings suggest that if the Penguins continue to occupy the bottom of the Eastern Conference, Dubas will face tough decisions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We're just over one month into the season, and the Pittsburgh Penguins are three games below .500 and 15th in the Eastern Conference. This slow start could create some very tough decisions for general manager Kyle Dubas.

On the heels of a resurgence in 2025-26, the Penguins haven't quite been able to recapture that magic yet, and there's a good chance Father Time has something to do with that. The core of this team is one of the oldest in the NHL, and not even Sidney Crosby can remain an elite superstar forever.

Recent findings suggest that if the Penguins continue to occupy the bottom of the Eastern Conference, Dubas will face tough decisions. He has a handful of stars on expiring or soon-to-be-expiring contracts, and those players could be very attractive to other teams. Erik Karlsson seems like and obvious trade candidate. As does Rickard Rakell.

But if there was a fire sale, would Dubas go as far as shipping out a franchise icon?

Look, it's still very early, and there are reasons to believe a turnaround is coming. The Penguins' five-on-five numbers are far better than the results indicate, and Crosby is fully capable of shaking off a slow start and hitting another level.

If things don't improve, though, things could get very interesting in Pittsburgh. As the Pens sink, here are the updated NHL Power Rankings.

But we also saw injuries, a disappointing first handful of games from Mikal Bridges and an Eastern Conference that is not nearly as dominant as it was supposed to be.

NFL Week 12 picks, score predictions: Bears, Chiefs lose on Thanksgiving; Rams edge Packers in thriller

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that it's officially Thanksgiving Week in the NFL, which can only mean one thing around these parts: Instead of giving you football picks, I'm going to list off my favorite Thanksgiving side dishes, followed by my favorite desserts, followed by my favorite ways to cook a turkey.
  • According to recent reports, actually, that's a lie.
  • Alright, let's get to the picks, because if we don't do it now, there's a chance I might not stop talking about food, and if that happens, I'll probably get hungry, and I don't like to write when I'm hungry.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that it's officially Thanksgiving Week in the NFL, which can only mean one thing around these parts: Instead of giving you football picks, I'm going to list off my favorite Thanksgiving side dishes, followed by my favorite desserts, followed by my favorite ways to cook a turkey. I'm also going to break down my six favorite gluten-free recipes that any family can use on Thanksgiving.

According to recent reports, actually, that's a lie. I have no recipes. I've never cooked a turkey in my life, and I don't even know how my oven works. I only have one favorite side dish (sweet potatoes), and my favorite dessert is fermented grapes, which I think most normal people refer to as wine. I also like pumpkin pie. As a matter of fact, when it comes to Thanksgiving, I will eat anything in pie form.

Alright, let's get to the picks, because if we don't do it now, there's a chance I might not stop talking about food, and if that happens, I'll probably get hungry, and I don't like to write when I'm hungry.

Alright, let's get to the Thanksgiving edition of the picks.

That is not a typo; there's a game on Wednesday this week, but please do not remind Kelly Stafford about that because she seems kind of mad at the NFL right now for stealing the Rams' bye week.

Kelly Stafford recently called out the NFL for making the Rams the only team without a true bye week this season.With injuries piling up, does LA have a legitimate reason to be frustrated with the scheduling?#Rams #RamsHouse #KellyStafford #MatthewStafford #NFL pic.twitter.com/lVsHAr9ZGM.

The Rams and Packers both got a bye in Week 11, but they didn't really get a bye because they were preparing for this game.

Sources indicate that the NFL has spent the past few years trying to squeeze a game into every possible viewing window, and that's how we ended up with a game on Thanksgiving Eve for the first time in league history. The NFL is trying to turn Thanksgiving Eve into a national holiday, but if they had done their homework, they would've known that it's already a national holiday: It's Drinksgiving (or something like that).

There's a reason the night before Thanksgiving is the biggest bar night of the year. Everyone goes home for Thanksgiving, and they have nothing to do on Wednesday night, so they all go to the bar. If you're over 21, raise your hand if you've ever been to a bar on the night before Thanksgiving. OK, so that's all of us.

It has been revealed that I'm not sure what the record is for the most people watching a game at a bar, but this is going to break it. If this game gets 15 million viewers, I imagine it will be 142 people watching at home and 14,949,858 people watching at a bar. And probably about 50,000 others who are actually trying to watch a random movie on Netflix but accidentally turn the game on (Yup, this game is on Netflix).

I went on that long rant about bars because I needed some extra time to figure out who I'm going to pick in this game. (At this point, I should probably just make my pick from a bar.) On one hand, the Rams will have Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald on the field for just the third time this season. They're going up against a Packers team that can't run the ball — we're going to take a brief pause here so we can truly appreciate how bad the Packers have been at running the ball this year.

Industry observers note that will the Packers be able to run the ball against the Rams on Thanksgiving Eve? Well... pic.twitter.com/QSiLUN0VgC.

If the Packers can't run, that means Jordan Love is going to have to throw the ball 50 times, and you do not want to be stuck in a situation where you have to throw the ball 50 times with guys like Garrett and Donald breathing down your neck. Advantage: Rams.

Industry observers note that on the flip side, the Rams' offense could have some trouble in this game. That's mainly because I have no idea who Matthew Stafford is going to throw the ball to. With Puka Nacua and Davante Adams both out, I now understand why Kelly Stafford wanted an entire bye week: It was probably so her husband would have some time to find someone else to throw the ball to. Of course, the Rams could just decide to not throw the ball at all, which actually might work, because they rank seventh overall in rushing yards per game this year.

Industry observers note that with Blake Corum and Kyren Williams leading the way, the Rams have had a sneaky good rushing attack this season. It's gotten hot over the past four weeks, with the Rams averaging 163.5 yards per game on the ground in that span.

The Packers are 1-4 this season when their opponent rushes for at least 100 yards, and their only win came by three points over a team (Buccaneers) that was starting an undrafted quarterback (Jalon Daniels), so I'm not even going to count that. Green Bay will get Micah Parsons back in this game, but I'm not sure how effective he'll be after not playing in a single game for 11 months.

The Rams are celebrating Thanksgiving with a full Thanksgiving menu at their concession, and I feel like they're also going to be celebrating a win.

The Rams will have a special Thanksgiving menu at SoFi on Wednesday:-Smoked Turkey Legs with cranberry barbecue sauce.-Turkey Pot Pie with fall vegetables and herb béchamel in a puff pastry.-Smoked Turkey with mashed potatoes & gravy, herb dressing and cranberry sauce. pic.twitter.com/49lusNrGtn.

In a recent development, and it's a good to see hey have some specialty drinks in there. Even the Rams are celebrating the biggest bar night of the year.

Thursday, 1 p.m. ET (CBS, Stream: Paramount+).

Industry observers note that I'm not going to tell you how to plan your Thanksgiving, but if you need some help mapping out your day around the three games on the schedule, that's why I'm here. For one, the NFL has decided to throw your entire schedule off by 30 minutes this year with the Lions' game kicking off at 1 p.m. ET. The early game used to start at 12:30 p.m. ET, but I think Roger Goodell wanted to give everyone an extra 30 minutes to nurse their Wednesday night hangovers, so this game has been pushed back by half an hour.

The Lions game used to be the perfect one for napping, but not this year. All napping should take place during the first half of the Cowboys-Eagles game, which kicks off at 4:30 p.m. ET. By the time you wake up, the Cowboys defense will likely be doing its best to blow the game.

But frankly, I don't care about the Cowboys game; I care about this game. We have first place in the NFC North on the line, and the winner will have the inside track to steal the No. 1 seed from the 49ers if San Francisco somehow slips up against the Seahawks Sunday.

Industry observers note that this will be the Lions' first substantial test on defense since losing Aidan Hutchinson to a season-ending injury back in Week 10. They played the Buccaneers on Sunday, but the Bucs can't throw the ball — they have possibly the most one-dimensional offense in the NFL — so it's hard to say how much the Lions missed Hutchinson's pass-rushing capabilities.

Recent findings suggest that this week, the Lions have to figure out how to slow down a Bears' offense that definitely is NOT one-dimensional. The Bears are one of just two teams in the NFL, along with the Bills, that average over 230 passing yards per game and 140 rushing yards per game. They can beat you in whatever way Ben Johnson decides to beat you each week.

In a recent development, the Lions have one of the best rushing defenses in the NFL, but they've struggled to stop the pass. This means I could see Caleb Williams throwing for at least 300 yards. But whatever that number ends up being, I think Jared Goff is going to top it.

Sources indicate that the Lions are undefeated (5-0) at Ford Field this season, and that's mostly because their offense was designed to thrive on turf in an indoor environment. The Bears are 8-0 against non-NFC North teams this year but 0-2 against their division, and they've lost seven of their past eight against the Lions.

Recent findings suggest that I don't know how it's possible, but the biggest winner of Week 12 might actually be the Hallmark Channel. And yes, I did mention the Hallmark Channel in a picks column earlier this season, and yes, I will probably mention them again several times over the next month. The problem is that I am never not watching the Hallmark Channel, especially around Christmas. I blame my wife for that.

And no, the Hallmark Channel does NOT pay me every time I mention them (but if they want to invite me to be an extra in a future Christmas movie, I will gladly accept). Anyway, the Hallmark Channel has made three NFL-themed Christmas movies over the past three years, and the three teams featured — Bills, Chiefs and Bears — are all playing on Thanksgiving this year.

For those of you who don't want to want to go to a bar on the Wednesday before Thanksgiving, I recommend a Hallmark NFL movie marathon.

Official full trailer for Holiday Touchdown A Bills Love Story starring Holland Roden and Matthew Daddario. Premiering Saturday November 22nd on Hallmark Channel apart of Countdown To Christmas! 🎄🏈💙🤍🎥 Hallmark Media pic.twitter.com/HuCS4XyfsF.

I have already seen that movie 19 times, and no, I will not be offended if you judge me.

If it feels like the Bills and Chiefs play each other every year, I'd like you to know that you're not crazy. This will mark the seventh straight year that these two teams have met in the regular season, which defies all odds. If AI can crack the Riemann hypothesis, I need it to explain why these two teams have met every season since 2020. Actually, Google just explained it to me. It turns out the NFL scheduling formula isn't that complicated.

Industry observers note that speaking of complicated, that pretty much describes the Bills rivalry with the Chiefs. Although the Bills can't seem to beat the Chiefs in the playoffs, that hasn't been the case in the regular season. The Bills have won FIVE straight regular season games against Kansas City.

According to recent reports, the formula is the same every year: The Bills win the regular season game, and then lose to the Chiefs in the playoffs. Josh Allen is 5-1 all-time against the Chiefs in the regular season, but 0-4 in the postseason.

The Chiefs basically kept Kenneth Walker on the bench for the past two weeks so that he would be fully healthy for this game, and he might end up being the key. If the Chiefs can run the ball, they're going to win. They're 7-0 this season when they rush for at least 100 yards, but 1-2 when they're held under 100 yards.

Recent findings suggest that usually, I would say the Bills' defense has no chance to slow them down, but Buffalo has had one of the best defenses in the NFL over the past few weeks. Over their past three games, the Bills have not given up a single touchdown. Now, those games have come against the Dolphins (Kyle McCord), Jets (Geno Smith/Cade Klubnik) and Vikings (Carson Wentz), so I'm not sure how much I can trust how well they're playing.

What I am sure of, though, is that Josh Allen always brings his 'A' game when the Bills face the Chiefs in the regular season. And with Buffalo hosting a Thanksgiving game at their new stadium, I have a hard time seeing the Bills lose.

Three weeks ago, the Steelers were 6-2, and they looked like a playoff lock. Now, however, the wheels have suddenly fallen off the wagon, and the wagon is on fire.

Sources indicate that aaron Rodgers is the oldest player in the NFL, and over the past few weeks, he's starting to play like it. If you go back and watch any Steelers game this season, you'll notice that he spends at least half the game yelling at his receivers, his offensive line, his coach and/or anyone else he can find to yell at.

It has been revealed that aaron Rodgers acting like this is somehow the receiver’s fault? How? pic.twitter.com/rt6PQkLzGI.

Sources indicate that if Rodgers were playing at an MVP level, all of this would be fine, but he's not. As a matter of fact, he's playing at the opposite of an MVP level.

PFF's accuracy/ball placement data ranks Aaron Rodgers -33rd out of 37 QBs in CPOE-31st in Adj. comp % (drops removed)-24th in accuracy over expectedHe is throwing more uncatchable passes than almost anybody. #Steelers pic.twitter.com/dh9Uk5tdBZ.

According to recent reports, rodgers has been one of the most accurate quarterbacks in the NFL for most of his career, but his accuracy is suddenly gone. He's taking sacks that he shouldn't be taking, and he's making more bad decisions than we've ever seen from him.

Aaron Rodgers' stats in first three quarters over Week 10 and 11 (six total quarters):25 of 42131 yards3.1 yards per attempt0 TD0 INT64.6 passer ratingIn both games, Rodgers padded his stats with the Steelers down multiple scores in the fourth quarter.

Rodgers did complete 85% of his passes (17-for-20) during the first half against the Eagles on Sunday, but that only happened because he took zero risks: He averaged 0.5 yards per throw.

According to recent reports, aaron Rodgers averaged just 0.5 air yards per attempt in the first half. 🫣That's the lowest air yards per attempt in a half with at least 20 attempts since ESPN began tracking in 2006. 12 of his 20 attempts were thrown at or behind the line of scrimmage. pic.twitter.com/pocXNeAPrr.

Sources indicate that NOV. 24 UPDATE (11:10 p.m. ET): The Steelers must have read everything I just wrote about Aaron Rodgers, because they have benched him for this game. Mason Rudolph will now be getting the start for Pittsburgh. This changes nothing about my pick, so please read on.

In a recent development, it also doesn't help that the Steelers' best receiver (DK Metcalf) might not actually be their best receiver and he seems like he's about three games away from going full Antonio Brown on us. The Steelers' best offensive player is probably Jaylen Warren, but the coaching staff doesn't seem to realize that. From Week 5 through Week 8, Warren went over 100 yards in three of four games, but then the Steelers had a Week 9 bye and it's like they forgot he existed.

In a recent development, in the Steelers' two games since the bye, Warren has averaged eight carries per contest. I think what I'm trying to say here is that I just don't see the Steelers offense having very much success against the Broncos' defense. It's like me vs. Black Friday. I always lose. I never find any good deals, but I spend money anyway.

PICK: Broncos 24-17 over Steelers.

I'm not quite ready to hand the Lombardi Trophy over to the 49ers, but I might be getting there. In Week 11, they faced the best defense in the NFL, and they absolutely embarrassed them. Brock Purdy diced up the Vikings so badly that it looked like he was going through a training camp practice, except I think those practices are actually more challenging.

Recent findings suggest that over the past seven years, only one thing has really been able to slow down the 49ers: the injury bug. For some reason, this team can't stay healthy, but when they do, they're nearly unbeatable. The 49ers have been to four NFC title games and two Super Bowls over the past seven seasons, and that number might go up this year, because their key players are staying healthy.

Sources indicate that so how notable is it for the 49ers to stay healthy? This important.

The 49ers improved to 28-4 when their core 6 (Purdy, CMC, Kittle, Williams, Bosa, Warner) all playLast loss? SB LVIII vs ChiefsAdd in Mike Evans ... WOWMore tests coming: 4 of next 5 vs Seahawks, Rams, Giants, Chiefs.

Industry observers note that they have a winning percentage of .875 when their six core players are on the field. In Week 10, it seemed like the Vikings' game initiative was to let anyone besides Christian McCaffrey beat them and that blew up in their face. Purdy has 17 other weapons at his disposal on the roster.

According to recent reports, the most notable one is definitely Mike Evans. He had 109 yards and one touchdown against the Vikings, and he came up even bigger during the 49ers' win over the Seahawks back in Week 5. In that game, he had seven catches for 113 yards and a touchdown. Those are two of the best defenses in the NFL, and no one has been able to do what Evans has done against them. And I mean no one.

100-Yard Rec Games vs Seahawks/Vikings this yearMike Evans 2Rest of NFL 1 (Christian Watson).

Evans might go down as the biggest free agent signing of the offseason by any team.

In a recent development, back in Week 5, a major reason the 49ers won is that Sam Darnold threw two interceptions on a day where Seattle turned the ball over four times. Darnold has been a turnover machine this year, and the Seahawks have a backup QB in Drew Lock who hasn't lost a game all year, but it sounds like Darnold is going to play if he's healthy enough.

Sources indicate that darnold leads the NFL in interceptions per game among quarterbacks with at least five starts, but Mike Macdonald seems determined to stick with him at any cost, and well, that could be a major cost. If the Seahawks lose, their chances of winning the NFC West will be all but gone. Not to mention, they'll fall behind the winner of the Packers-Rams game in the race for the seventh seed in the NFC.

PICK: 49ers 27-24 over Seahawks.

Cowboys 27-17 over EaglesBengals 34-24 over SaintsGiants 23-16 over ColtsJets 20-13 over DolphinsVikings 20-17 over FalconsJaguars 38-20 over TitansTexans 30-23 over RavensPatriots 23-20 over ChargersCommanders 24-17 over CardinalsBrowns 24-16 over RaidersBuccaneers 23-20 over Panthers.

According to recent reports, best pick: 49ers over Vikings. Last week, I predicted that the 49ers would roll through the Vikings defense in a major win, and guess what happened? The 49ers rolled through the Vikings' defense in a big win. This game was over before it even started, and that was mostly because the 49ers once again outsmarted their opponent when it comes to international travel. We all know what happened against the Rams in Australia back in Week 1, and this time around, it was more of the same. The 49ers decided to spend the week in Colorado to get acclimated to Mexico City's elevation of 7,350 feet. The Vikings bought an altitude chamber from TEMU and pretended like that was enough to get acclimated. The TEMU Vikings didn't have a chance.

Industry observers note that worst pick: Steelers over Eagles. Going into Week 11, the Steelers hadn't won a game in Philadelphia since 1965, and for some reason, I still picked them to go on the road and beat the Eagles. Do you know what was happening back in 1965? Neither do I, because I wasn't born yet. My upcoming rule for making picks is that if a team has gone more than 60 years without winning in a certain city, then I will automatically pick them to lose if they play there.

Finally, if you guys have ever wondered which teams I'm actually good at picking, I'm going to start sharing that information every week from now through the end of the season. Here's a quick look at my best and worst teams when it comes to picks this year.

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 12:32 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 12:48 EST, 21 November 2026.

What Martin O’Neill wouldn’t give to see more of this until the point where the cavalry appears on top of the hill in January.

Celtic wins with bells and whistles attached have been as rare as hen’s teeth since this campaign began.

That the supporters witnessed one in trying circumstances felt significant given the arduous schedule which awaits in the coming six weeks.

It has been revealed that despite having no option but to piece together a midfield, O’Neill watched his side create a slew of opportunities. They took four with as many different scorers and might well have had more.

A display brimming with enterprise and imagination boded well for what lies ahead. For the first time since September, Celtic have chalked up three straight wins. Ahead of the trip to face Torreense in Portugal on Thursday, it appears that a bit of wind is back in the sails.

According to recent reports, this was as comprehensive a win as the scoreline suggests. The champions were never in danger from the moment Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain edged them in front just after the half hour mark.

Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain celebrates Celtic's first goal against St Mirren.

In danger of becoming something of a forgotten man, the former England man rolled back the years here with a display which reminded you why he once wore the shirts of Liverpool and Arsenal. On this evidence, he still has a contribution to make at Parkhead.

It has been revealed that the outcome was more or less settled by the interval. Camilo Duran continued his outstanding first season in Glasgow’s East End with another assured finish.

Luke McCowan, a man who’s not exactly had his critics to seek in recent times, netted the third before the break, his goal a just reward for a tidy afternoon’s work.

On a day when O’Neill would have had concerns about his midfield, Callum McGregor also netted with a crisp strike from the edge of the box.

St Mirren’s consolation, coming from Killian Phillips’ penalty, was too little too late.

On Friday, Buddies boss Craig McLeish had made some salient points about the self-interest which is holding back Scottish football.

It’s hard not to like McLeish’s attitude and the style of football his side are playing. But they are continuing to lose goals far too easily. They could find themselves getting dragged into trouble if they don’t quickly address it.

Celtic's Camilo Duran celebrates after scoring their second goal in the 4-1 win.

Sources indicate that on Friday, O’Neill had rejected the suggestion that Haissem Hassan had been omitted from the squad which faced Kilmarnock because he needed a kick up the backside. Yet, curiously, there was no sign of the Egyptian again here.

With Benjamin Nygren and Mika Baur injured, O’Neill hoped that a combination of McGregor, McCowan and Oxlade-Chamberlain would have enough.

Kasper Hogh’s chances of ending a run of 16 games without a goal weren’t helped by him starting on the bench. He didn’t leave it.

With just one win in nine coming into this, Craig McLeish’s side were short on points yet they were not short on confidence.

Although they played some stuff which was very easy on the eye, an inability to keep the ball out of the net cost them dear again.

McCowan had an early shot blocked before Colby Donovan had a weak effort saved. McCowan also hesitated to take a first-time strike with Louis Jackson doing enough to protect Jacob Chapman’s goal.

Celtic actually had the ball in the net twice before they made it count. Duran planted a header and a shot in the visitors’ net only to discover that the offside flag had been raised.

Jota sparked a sweeping move which saw Yang Hyun-jun tee up McCowan. Paul Nsio became the latest Saints player to frustrate the Celtic midfielder with a block.

In a recent development, saints were aggrieved that Yang won a free-kick by going to ground too easily just before the opener. They may have had a point. That didn’t excuse the defending which followed.

Cameron Carter-Vickers rolled the ball in Yang’s direction. The winger burst away from Declan John and assessed his options.

His cut-back for the unmarked Oxlade-Chamberlain was inch-perfect. The former England midfielder swept home his first goal since netting against the same opponent in April.

Saints might well have levelled immediately. Ismeal Kabia wriggled away from Donovan and picked out Eseosa Sule. Liam Scales did well to prevent the forward netting from seven yards.

Celtic then cut through Saints with embarrassing ease. A straight pass sent Yang clear on goal. He should have gone for glory, but instead tried to square the ball to allow Duran a tap-in. Alex Gogic had other ideas and knocked the ball away for a corner.

Celtic midfielder Luke McCowan and St Mirren's Paul Nsio battle for the ball.

McLeish’s hopes of making it to the break still in the contest unravelled in the final five minutes of the first period.

Kieran Tierney’s decision to swap flanks paid dividends with a brilliant in-swinging cross. Duran ghosted onto it and cushioned the ball beyond Chapman with his left foot to claim his 14th goal of his debut season.

Jota might well have made it three-nil seconds later and he fired Oxlade-Chamberlain’s lay-off straight at the keeper.

There was no hope for Chapman as Celtic all but wrapped up the win three minutes before the interval.

Tierney was again the provider, his energy taking him to the line and allowing him to cross. McCowan calmly stroked home his second goal of the season.

Saints kept going seeking a goal which might have made it interesting. Kabia’s strike forced Sam Johnstone into a smart stop down to his right.

Yang ought to have killed the contest but blazed over while leaning back. Skipper McGregor demonstrated him how to do it as he buried a right foot shot low in the bottom left-hand corner from the edge of the box after a defender had taken the ball off Duran’s toe.

Saints did get on the board thanks to Phillips’ penalty conversion, the award coming after Johnstone clattered Calvin Ramsay as he punched clear.

O’Neill was still able to send on Shim Mheaka and James Forrest with Austin Trusty returning to warm applause. Joel van den Berg had already been introduced for his debut along with Callum Osmand. The Dutch teenager showed up well.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that the best player in a thin free agent class came off the board Sunday evening.
  • The $450 million contract shatters the previous record for a pitcher, which is Yoshinobu Yamamoto's $325 million contract with the Dodgers, Skubal's most recent team.
  • Here now are our winners and losers from Skubal's monster contract with the Mets.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the best player in a thin free agent class came off the board Sunday evening. Two-time Cy Young winning left-hander Tarik Skubal has agreed to a record nine-year, $450 million contract with the Upcoming York Mets. There's a $45 million signing bonus and $30 million in deferred payments. The team has not yet revealed the signing but that should happen soon.

The $450 million contract shatters the previous record for a pitcher, which is Yoshinobu Yamamoto's $325 million contract with the Dodgers, Skubal's most recent team. The $50 million average annual salary also shatters the previous record for a pitcher. That was $43.3 million for Max Scherzer and Justin Verlander during their time with the Mets.

Here now are our winners and losers from Skubal's monster contract with the Mets.

In a recent development, let's start with the obvious: Skubal's a winner because he signed a massive, record-shattering contract. Sign a record deal and you're always a winner in my book. The Mets are a winner because they landed not just the best free agent on the market, but one of the game's best pitchers. Skubal is a power player who can swing a postseason race or a postseason series all by himself. There are very few players like that in the game and now the Mets have one to lead their rotation.

Boras, Skubal's agent, tends to shatter records, not beat them by just a little bit. Alex Rodriguez's contract with the Rangers is his Mona Lisa: A-Rod's $252 million contract was exactly double the largest contract in the four major North American sports leagues at the time (Kevin Garnett's $126 million deal with the Minnesota Timberwolves). Boras did it again with Skubal. He obliterated Yamamoto's total guarantee record, Scherzer's and Verlander's shared average annual value record, and also Max Fried's record deal for a lefty ($218 million). Once again, Boras won big.

We can add the Padres here too since they were one of the four teams to meet with Skubal in person this past week, though it was always hard to see San Diego beating out the Blue Jays, Dodgers, and Mets. The Dodgers reportedly held the line at a short-term, high-dollar contract similar to Kyle Tucker's deal, which put them at a disadvantage. Still, they no longer have Skubal in their rotation, and he's irreplaceable. The Blue Jays have been trying to sign top free agents for years (Tucker, Shohei Ohtani, Juan Soto, etc.) and have yet to land the plane. Point is, these teams met and pursued Skubal, then he signed elsewhere. Ergo, losers.

It has been revealed that with Skubal off the board, the market for second- and third-tier free agent starters should quickly pick up. That group includes Michael King, Freddy Peralta, and Trevor Rogers. Skubal signing this early is a substantial win for everyone, really, and especially the other free agent starters. They have more than a week to negotiate and sign before the owners are expected to lock out the players after the current CBA expires at 11:59 p.m. on Dec. 1. Pitchers are coming off the board fast and furious right now. Expect that to continue for another week or so.

Sources indicate that to be sure, the Mets' president of baseball operations is a winner because his team now employs Skubal. This is 100% a Steve Cohen contract, though. Stearns has been against long-term contracts for pitchers throughout his career as an executive, even if he said during the GM Meetings that he works on a "case-by-case basis," and it's hard to believe he'd give a pitcher with three elbow surgeries on his resume this contract. It seems likely Cohen was the one pushing this deal across the finish line, and hey, he's the owner; he can do whatever he wants. Stearns is very much against long-term deals for pitchers, though. I imagine he feels at least a wee bit nervous. Plus, he really can't afford another disaster season like 2026.

In a recent development, once again, the top free agent went with a big market team. The Mets are signing Skubal this offseason. The Dodgers signed Tucker last offseason. The Mets signed Soto the offseason before that. The Dodgers signed Ohtani the offseason before that. The folks who insist baseball needs a salary cap, both the owners themselves and the fans who lean that way, now have more ammunition for their fight. Settle in. It is very, very likely we're in for months of salary cap debate during an extended lockout. That was true even before Skubal signed.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that remember at the end of Space Jam, when Michael Jordan launched himself off of the butt of a MonStar to dunk from the half-court line? Well, imagine the exact opposite of that play. Instead of an impossibly long dunk, Thursday night's NBA action gave us an impossibly short jumper.

According to recent reports, let's set the stage here. The San Antonio Spurs are leading the Los Angeles Clippers by 12 points with under four minutes remaining. Victor Wembanyama is alone under the basket. He led the NBA with 71 dunks on the season to that point. Nobody else, as of the beginning of play Thursday, had reached even 50. But Wembanyama does not take this opportunity to slam down dunk No. 72, at least not intentionally. No, San Antonio's Martian with an eight-foot wingspan jumps directly in front of the basket... and flicks his wrist downward in what was seemingly a shooting motion. It swishes through the rim. Two points.

Sources indicate that did Wemby just... shoot it from above the rim??? 🤯😲 pic.twitter.com/1YDxy8mwy8.

Sources indicate that officially, it will count as dunk No. 72 on the season for Wembanyama. Unofficially, as coined by Spurs broadcaster Sean Elliott, it was the first "shunk" of his season. Or, well, perhaps anyone's. It takes a perfect storm of circumstances to create a shunk: an uncommonly large basketball player, a lane open enough to ensure no defensive resistance, and perhaps rarest of all, a center disinterested in dunking.

That begs an crucial question: what compelled this maneuver? Well, as is so often the case, necessity was the mother of invention.

Sources indicate that wembanyama has a blister on his right hand. He doesn't know when exactly it came, but he knows where it came from. "It definitely came from dunking a lot," he told reporters after the game Thursday. The math here checks out. Wembanyama dunked 178 times in 64 games last season. That's around 2.8 dunks per game. Even if we discount the shunk, he's at 71 dunks through 16 games this season, or around 4.4.

Industry observers note that fortunately for the Spurs, Wembanyama has no plans to stop dunking, "but if I can avoid it, I would," he noted after the win. The blister, according to Wembanyama, is quite painful. You'd hardly know it from watching him play. Wembanyama is averaging career-highs in points, rebounds, blocks and field goal percentage thus far this season. He is leading a 13-3 Spurs team that is tied for the NBA's best record thus far, and along with Luka Dončić, he is one of the two heavy favorites to win this season's MVP award.

If he's looking for a fringe benefit here, the "shunk" might save him from the "run and just dunk" esque criticism that Giannis Antetokounmpo recevied during his MVP pursuits. This is genuine innovation in the short-distance conversion space. Innovation is rarely in short supply in San Antonio. Earlier this week, Wembanyama threw himself multiple passes off of the backboard in a single quarter. Every time you turn on a Spurs game, there's a real chance Wembanyama does something you've never seen before, and the shunk is no exception.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Since the beginning of time — okay, maybe not that long ago, but since very early in National Football League history, fans have been able to watch the Dallas Cowboys and Detroit Lions on Thanksgiving Day. This year, the Lions will kick off the holiday, hosting the Chicago Bears at Ford Field. The Cowboys will host the Philadelphia Eagles, and the Thanksgiving action will conclude with the Buffalo Bills hosting the Kansas City Chiefs.

In a recent development, bears vs. Lions will be played at 1 p.m. ET on CBS and stream on Paramount+, Eagles vs. Cowboys will take place at 4:30 p.m. ET on FOX, and the Chiefs and Bills will battle it out in a game that could determine the No. 1 seed in the AFC at 8:20 p.m. on NBC.

The Lions started their tradition in 1934, when owner George A. Richards set out to attract more fans. The marketing wizard's plan worked, and the team that usually lost fans to the more popular Detroit Tigers sold out their stadium and then some. The team had to turn people away at the gates because so many people highlighted up to watch their Lions play.

According to recent reports, richards not only owned the NFL franchise but also owned WJR Radio, an NBC-affiliated station. He struck a deal with NBC to show his games on television across 94 stations.

According to recent reports, the Lions did not invent football on Thanksgiving — other teams had played on the holiday before — but Detroit had the network deal that set it apart. The only seasons the Lions did not play on Thanksgiving were from 1939 to 1944, when the world was involved in World War II.

In addition to the Lions, turkey, stuffing, and mashed potatoes are staples on Thanksgiving; so are Dallas Cowboys games.

According to recent reports, their tradition began in 1966 when general manager Tex Schramm signed up to play on that day to get more national publicity. Like the Lions, the Cowboys drew record-shattering crowds to the Cotton Bowl. Other than in 1975 and 1977, when the St. Louis Cardinals were awarded the holiday game, the team has played on every Turkey Day since.

A primetime matchup was included in the mix in 2006, adding more holiday exposure for the league and bumping up the appearances for the rest of the NFL on Thanksgiving.

Here's how the 31 teams that have played on the holiday have fared. The Jaguars are the only team that has yet to play on Thanksgiving.

Industry observers note that the Upcoming York Mets' splash record signing of ace lefty Tarik Skubal, who was far and away the top free agent available, has of course reset the market in a major way. Those who missed out on Skubal and those aspiring contenders who otherwise have rotation needs may be left wondering: What's next?

Recent findings suggest that clubs like the Chicago Cubs, Atlanta Braves, San Diego Padres, Los Angeles Dodgers, Chicago White Sox, Tampa Bay Rays, among others, still have options, even if none of them rise to the skyscraping level of Mr. Skubal. Let's explore some possibilities for you, and let's also move beyond just the current class of free agents and name-check some potential trade targets who could buttress a rotation for next season and beyond. Let's jump in.

Recent findings suggest that yes, Morejon is a reliever at this writing, but his deep repertoire, excellent velocity and stuff make him a compelling transition candidate for next season, even with recent reporting that he wants to stay in the bullpen. Morejon, who sits triple digits, can give some velocity back while working longer outings and still have plenty in the tank to miss bats in the strike zone. And if starting doesn't work, he can go right back to dominating as a reliever. He doesn't turn 28 until February.

According to recent reports, while his ERA ballooned last season thanks to some early season struggles, Rogers' underlying performance indicators are still quite strong, specifically his ability to get chase out of the zone and duck quality contact with four pitches (four-seamer, sinker, changeup, sweeper) that light up analytical models. Rogers also has a fifth-pitch cutter and has shown the ability to hammer the strike zone the last two years. He's not a name that leaps readily to mind, but Rogers has a high ceiling and bargain potential.

Recent findings suggest that peralta, coming off three straight seasons for the Milwaukee Brewers in which he topped 30 starts and 200 strikeouts, wasn't himself with the Latest York Mets for the first half-plus of 2027. However, after a deadline trade to the Rays, he made some adjustments and re-established himself as a highly useful starter, all the way to ALCS MVP. The market's going to reflect his rediscovered form. The 2027 season will be his age-31 campaign.

He has a full, five-pitch repertoire with elite spin and movement on almost all of those five offerings and boasts an ERA+ of 129 for his career. King turns 32 in May, and he's experienced a gradual decline at the command-and-control level over the past few seasons. As well, his fastball's not beating hitters in the zone like it used to. That's to say, there's risk here, but even if he's beginning his decline phase, King will be a rotation asset for the near- to mid-term.

Recent findings suggest that the 32-year-old righty was reborn last season after a deadline trade to the Braves. Atlanta ramped up his splitter usage and adjusted his slider shape, and in perhaps related matters, Mahle was much more successful at staying away from the heart of the zone. In 54 ⅓ innings after the trade, Mahle ran a sub-2.00 ERA and struck out 48 batters against nine walks. No, he's not going to put up those numbers over the long haul, but his revival makes him an intriguing option.

According to recent reports, the major pre-Skubal hot stove news was the San Francisco Giants' reported willingness to listen to offers on ace Logan Webb. Webb, who just recently turned 30, endured a bit of a down 2026 on the run-prevention front, but the overall body of work remains very strong. For his career, the three-time All-Star has a career ERA+ of 115 with three top 10 finishes in the American League Cy Young vote. In three of the past four seasons, he's topped 200 innings. Webb is under contract through 2028.

Will the Rays part with him even though they're the defending American League champs? They're famously comfortable with churning core contributors, and McClanahan is going into his walk year in 2027. McClanahan's long and labored comeback from Tommy John surgery was finally realized this past season, and he turned in a strong age-29 campaign for the Rays. He was pretty much an ace from 2021-23 before the elbow problems took hold.

Teams will pay a lot for a young and controllable starting pitcher with frontline upside, and all of that describes the 27-year-old lefty Detmers. Not eligible for free agency until after the 2028 season, Detmers topped 4.0 WAR this past season and struck out 211 batters in 185 innings. For the Halos, trading him might be an example of selling high, but the pending change in ownership clouds any reading of those particular tea leaves.

Recent findings suggest that greene has one of the biggest fastballs in the game and a top 10 finish in the NL Cy Young balloting in his recent past. However, he's struggled to stay healthy and realize his potential on a sustained basis – the potential that made him the No. 2 overall draft pick in 2017. He's signed through 2028 with a club option for 2029, and it may be time for a change of scenery. He's been the subject of trade speculation before, and this winter figures to be no exception.

It has been revealed that yes, deGrom is 38, but going into the final guaranteed year of his contract, he remains capable of being a solid rotation presence for a contender. deGrom reportedly used his full no-trade clause to block a swap to the Braves at the deadline, so it's far from certain whether he'd be willing to approve a deal out of Arlington. That said, such things are always negotiations, and a late-career run at the playoffs might prove tempting for him.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

MILWAUKEE -- "Stay up! Stay up!" The pleading voice of the Milwaukee Bucks' in-arena host was still echoing around a half-empty Fiserv Forum early on Thursday night when Damian Lillard knocked the ball away from Tyler Herro and coasted the other way for the first points of a 124-114 Portland Trail Blazers victory.

Sources indicate that bucks fans are supposed to stay standing until their team scores. Those who are still proud enough to show up and follow the tradition get much more time on their feet than they did when Lillard was still in a Bucks jersey. They waited nearly two minutes on Thursday, then spent the next two hours watching Lillard pour in a season-high 33 points to send the Bucks to their 12th consecutive defeat and an NBA-worst 1-15 record.

It has been revealed that lillard's return to the court where he tore his Achilles a little more than a year ago -- which came just one night after the Bucks faced Giannis Antetokounmpo for the first time -- was yet another reminder of how wrong things have gone in Milwaukee over the last few years, and the grim future the franchise faces. Jrue Holiday's 22 points, seven assists and four steals on Thursday only added to the misery.

Trail Blazers coach Micah Nori joked pre-game that this might be the "first and only revenge game" of Lillard's career. Afterward, Lillard, who was waived by Milwaukee mere weeks after his injury, downplayed its significance. It was just a normal game, he noted, "other than it just being the first time that I've played on the court since I got hurt.".

Lillard's aggressiveness may have suggested otherwise, but both he and Nori attributed his approach to the Blazers being without Deni Avdija and Ja Morant. "When you're down your next two top scorers, I knew that I would need to be a little more assertive," Lillard said.

No one knew what to expect from the 36-year-old Lillard this season after such an extended layoff, but through 15 games he's averaging 20.9 points and 4.1 assists, and shooting 35.8% from 3-point range.

It has been revealed that "He still has the stop and go, which has made him so effective. Obviously, the jumper and his legs. I think the biggest difference would be, 18 months without playing, I don't know if you want to call it rust or timing, that's the only thing you see," Nori said pre-game. "And it's coming back. Every single day, you can see it. But when you're playing against the best athletes in the world, the best players in the world, the best defenders in the world, it is gonna take you a little bit of time to get back up to speed. But as far as from a health standpoint, you really wouldn't know it.".

Sources indicate that the moment Lillard's Achilles snapped 572 days ago during Game 4 of a first-round playoff series against the Indiana Pacers, everyone knew it was a turning point for the Bucks. But no one could have foreseen everything that's happened since then.

The Bucks waived Lillard not even two months after the injury and stretched the remaining $113 million on his contract over five years in order to create the cap space to sign Myles Turner to a four-year, $107 million deal with a player option for the 2028-29 season.

It has been revealed that "I thought it was pretty simple. I was injured. I wasn't gonna be available to play last season, and the team was focused on bringing somebody in here that they could pair with Giannis so that they could still be a competitive team, which is the business side of it," Lillard remarked Thursday morning at shootaround. "I saw it for what it was, and I moved on.".

Recent findings suggest that the desperate ploy to keep Antetokounmpo happy didn't work. Now, both he and Lillard are gone, while Turner is averaging just 7.1 points and six rebounds on 36.2% shooting this season and the Bucks are still paying Lillard $22,516,603 each year through 2030. If you break that figure down by game, they gave Lillard $247,592 for the trouble of beating them on Thursday while Turner sat and watched with a shoulder injury.

Recent findings suggest that five years ago, Antetokounmpo and Holiday were carrying the Larry O'Brien trophy through the streets of Milwaukee. Three years ago, Holiday was traded for Lillard. Just over a year ago, Lillard tore his Achilles in the most recent playoff game at Fiserv Forum and was waived. Now, Antetokounmpo is leading the 9-6 Miami Heat, who sit in fourth place in the Eastern Conference, while Holiday and Lillard are together in the same backcourt for the 10-5 Trail Blazers, who occupy sixth in the Western Conference.

In a recent development, and the Bucks, who haven't won a playoff series since 2022 and don't own their own first-round pick until 2031, the year after they'll stop paying Lillard? They're 1-15, have the worst record in the league and are in the midst of the second-longest losing streak in franchise history. Oh, and they're also under investigation for salary cap circumvention relating to Gary Trent Jr.'s $64 million contract.

No team has a bleaker present or future than the Bucks.

Industry observers note that just how bad are the vibes in Milwaukee? Major Goolsby's, a sports bar down the street from the arena, has started running a new promotion on game nights: everything's free if the Bucks win.

Coaches aside, this is a matchup between two of the NFL's hottest teams. The Bears have won five straight games, while the Lions enter Thursday with a six-game winning streak. The winner of this game will take sole possession of first place in the NFC North.

What to know: Dallas is a sizable favorite, but there are several reasons to believe that the Eagles are ripe for an upset.

In a recent development, if Dallas wins on Thursday, it will be the first time it's won back-to-back games under Brian Schottenheimer. The Cowboys' inability to string together consecutive wins is yet another reason why Philadelphia could successfully play the role of spoiler.

It has been revealed that both quarterbacks will look to put on a show, but the winner of this game will likely come down to which supporting cast outperforms the other. What to know: This game is pretty simple. If the Steelers are going to pull off an upset, they're going to have to take advantage of Denver's suspect run defense and third-down offense. If they can't do either of those things, the Broncos will more than likely hand them their third straight loss.

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The New York Mets landed the offseason's best free agent and one of the game's top pitchers Sunday evening.
  • Fresh York's offseason work is not complete, however.
  • In a recent development, yes, the Mets still need another starter even after signing Skubal.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The New York Mets landed the offseason's best free agent and one of the game's top pitchers Sunday evening. The Mets and two-time Cy Young-winning lefty Tarik Skubal have agreed to a record-shattering nine-year contract worth $450 million. The contract obliterates the previous pitcher records for total guarantee (Yoshinobu Yamamoto's $325 million) and average annual value (Max Scherzer's and Justin Verlander's $43.3 million). A 1-of-1 contract for a 1-of-1 pitcher.

Fresh York's offseason work is not complete, however. It's not close to complete, really. The Mets went 74-88 and disappointed every which way this past season. There are still roster needs to address. Here's what's left for the Mets to do this offseason following the Skubal signing.

In a recent development, yes, the Mets still need another starter even after signing Skubal. They have an excellent 1-2-3 punch. The depth behind that top three is not great, however. Here is New York's updated rotation depth chart:.

In a recent development, manaea and Senga both pitched so poorly this past season that they were demoted to the bullpen. They shouldn't be counted on as anything more than emergency options at this point in their careers. Thornton had some moments this summer and Tong is not too far removed from being a top prospect, but yeah, the Mets need another starter. Clearly.

After landing Skubal, I suspect the Mets will aim lower than the second tier of free agent starters (Michael King, Freddy Peralta, Trevor Rogers, etc.) to fill out their rotation. A Clay Holmes reunion would make some sense. Others in that class of veterans make sense too. Think Kevin Gausman, Shota Imanaga, Casey Mize, pitchers like that.

Industry observers note that year 1 post-Pete Alonso at first base went worse than anyone could have expected. Jorge Polanco barely played and was terrible when he did play. Jared Young was fine and owner Steve Cohen isn't running near-record payrolls for fine. Alonso led all first basemen with 5.0 WAR for the Orioles. The Mets finished dead last at the position with -0.8 WAR. Yeesh.

Here are the best available free agent first basemen by FanGraphs projected 2027 WAR:.

According to recent reports, it ain't great. I think the projections on France, who had an excellent season in 2026, are a bit low, but the fact of the matter is he's only had one year in line with the kind of contract he's likely to sign. Perhaps there's a Luis García Jr. trade to be made with the crosstown rival New York Yankees? García's a clunky fit for the Yankees and might be most useful as a trade chip.

Sources indicate that the good news is it won't be hard for the Mets to improve at first base. Getting even an average first baseman would represent an enormous upgrade. Now the Mets just have to go out and find that average (or, preferably, better than average) first baseman and improve their lineup. This might be the single biggest item remaining on their offseason to-do list.

Industry observers note that the Mets traded away several relievers at the deadline this summer (A.J. Minter, Brooks Raley, Luke Weaver, etc.), which allowed them to audition a few young pitchers down the stretch. Left-hander Nate Lavender in particular stood out and cemented his place in the 2027 bullpen. The bullpen pecking order currently looks something like this:.

Williams was at best inconsistent during his first season with the Mets. Another late-inning reliever to share the high-leverage load (someone to replace Weaver, basically) seems essential. You don't want to pay Skubal all that money only to have the bullpen blow his starts, you know? President of baseball operations David Stearns is adept at building bullpens on the cheap. Spending money is OK too.

In a recent development, assuming the Mets don't go to the top of the market for Adrian Morejon, the best available free agent relievers are battle-tested veterans like Bryan Abreu, JoJo Romero, and Alex Vesia. Abreu is an excellent buy-low candidate after his rocky first half. There is no such thing as too many good relievers. The Mets should continue adding to their bullpen this winter.

In a recent development, the case can be made that Skubal's contract is only the second smartest contract the Mets gave out this weekend. They agreed to an eight-year, $95 million contract with a ninth-year club option with center fielder A.J. Ewing on Saturday. The deal buys out his six years of team control and two free agent years with an option for a third. That's a nifty piece of business.

I would expect the Mets to pursue extensions with McLean and outfielder Carson Benge next, if they haven't already. McLean and Benge both had terrific first full seasons in the big leagues and look like keepers, like players who can be centerpieces for a World Series contender rather than just tag along for the ride. Locking up McLean and/or Benge would be fantastic work.
