📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, the first thing to know about the 2027 draft cycle is that it remains wide open.
  • But after three full weeks of college basketball and heading into a Thanksgiving week full of high-profile matchups, we have updated the 2027 NBA Draft Significant Board.
  • Sources indicate that inside the front offices of the 30 NBA organizations, most have yet to even start ranking prospects.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the first thing to know about the 2027 draft cycle is that it remains wide open. There are still eight months to go before Adam Silver steps up to the podium to announce the first pick. Nothing has been decided yet. In fact, there's probably only about ten players total that can confidently say they expect to be a first-round pick at this point. Everything else is yet to be determined.

But after three full weeks of college basketball and heading into a Thanksgiving week full of high-profile matchups, we have updated the 2027 NBA Draft Significant Board.

Sources indicate that inside the front offices of the 30 NBA organizations, most have yet to even start ranking prospects. They're still building their lists, sorting them into tiers, and will spend the coming months trying to establish their order.

That's the biggest difference between those front offices and the public discourse about the draft. The fans want answers now, and the Twitter scouts are quick to make bold statements in hopes of saying they were right first. The experts who actually do this for a living recognize that the sole goal is to be right on draft night, and doing that requires them to not jump to any early conclusions.

That's all critical context to understanding this major board upgrade, which is, at best, a way too early look at the most relevant prospects. It should be interpreted in tiers. There are probably five or six prospects competing for the top of the draft, but that list could change. Maybe 11 who should feel good about their chances to be first-round picks. Everything beyond that is simply a battle that will continue to play out over the course of the next 8 months. Let's dive into the biggest storylines after three weeks of college basketball action.

I got a first-hand look at Stokes last week at the Player's Era 8 in Las Vegas. He went down with a contusion midway through his first game, sat out the second, and returned to drop 22 points and 11 rebounds in the final. In totality, the signs of extreme growth that have characterized his early season play continued to be evident in Vegas. He was far and away the most talented player in high school basketball a year ago, but had developed a history of not living up to his potential, or at least not impacting winning to the degree that someone with his talent should. So, coming into his year at Kansas, the eyeballs were more about his maturity, reliability, and approach. Answering those questions has gone about as well as it possibly could so far. He's not only been engaged and impactful, but he's shown connectivity with Bill Self that makes him look coachable. He's also not gotten easily derailed by adversity, which is a reassuring data point.

Industry observers note that to be clear, for as good as he's been, there's still plenty of room for improvement. In high school, he had an instinctive way of improvising his way to the rim. In college, he's found that isn't quite as easy, even with someone like Tre Kaufman-Renn regularly clearing the way for him anytime he comes charging at the rim. So, while he's over-dribbling at times, his playmaking is real, he's asserted himself as a rebounder, his shooting is progressing, and he's starting to use his size in the post.

The bottom line is this: most teams are looking for a potential alpha-type creator with the first pick. Stokes is your best bet in the 2027 cycle, by a relatively large margin at this point, but it's still too early to say he's a lock to go number one. I'd put that at about 70% at this point. Getting to the finish line will require him to continue trending in the right direction, making sure teams are comfortable with their due diligence in the pre-draft process, and also leaving open the possibility for someone else to emerge in the coming months.

It has been revealed that speaking of ascending prospects, no one has moved the needle more in the first three weeks of the season than Illinois' freshman Quentin Coleman. But for those who track draft prospects 365 days a year, the last three weeks are just a short spurt in what has been a rapid rise over the course of the last 15 months.

It has been revealed that in the 2025 EYBL season, Coleman averaged 11.8 points. 5.1 rebounds and 2.4 assists for a Brad Beal Elite team that won the Peach Jam Championship. To put it plainly, he was a role player, albeit a valuable one, on a team that was built around current Arkansas freshman JJ Andrews and utilized Trey Pearson, who is currently a freshman at High Point, as their primary ball-handler and distributor.

As soon as Coleman's high school season began, though, we immediately saw signs of growth. Those signs continued throughout the course of the year, and he skyrocketed the rankings in the process. He also decommitted from Wake Forest and took a much bigger NIL payday from Illinois. While he finished with five-star status, it was immediately clear at the USA Basketball trials in May that even that was too low.

Since arriving at Illinois, Coleman has continued the pattern of exceeding expectations. His skill level, feel for the game, defensive instincts, and nose for the ball are all as impressive as expected. The physical transition has been easier than expected. He's continued to develop more burst, physicality, and, as a result, playmaking.

At the moment, he's moved all the way up to No. 4 on the CBS's current 2027 NBA Draft Substantial Board, but we're not going to put a cap on what he could do given the unprecedented growth we've witnessed over the last 15 months.

In a recent development, there were a number of prospects who had a chance to be first-round picks in last year's draft, who opted to return to college basketball. While most, if not all, of them are probably making more money in college this year than they would have in the NBA, they are also making strides with their game, and in the process, helping their draft stock in what is widely viewed as a weaker draft than last year's.

Industry observers note that we've been bullish on Amari Allen's chances of helping himself given his new on-ball role at Alabama, and so far, he's done just that. The 16 points, 6 assists, and 5 rebounds per game on 52/50/82 shooting showcases both the versatility and shooting gains we were banking on. Most of all, though, it's his decision-making with the ball that has been glaring. His usage has gone way up, and his turnovers have gone way down. He has recorded 30 assists against just three turnovers through the first five games of the season. Add his hyper-competitiveness to the equation, and he's certainly helping himself.

Arizona big man Motiejus Krivas looked like an NBA-ready defender last year. This year, it's been more of the same. He's massive, even by NBA standards, at 7-foot-2 and 260 pounds, but deceptively versatile and very smart with his angles. We're also seeing definite growth offensively, particularly with his skill set facing the basket. Last week's 18-point, 12-rebound, 4-block performance against UConn was one that captured all of his value, and a game that scouts will undoubtedly revisit.

Industry observers note that meanwhile, his teammate, Ivan Kharchenkov, has gone from a defensive role player to Arizona's featured scorer, and is putting up nearly 23 points, 8 rebounds, and 5 assists per game. To put it plainly, he's been as good of a two-way player as there is in the country, and now looks like he could be trending towards the draft lottery.

In a recent development, florida's Thomas Haugh had a chance to be a mid-first-round pick last June, but the variable that gave many scouts pause was his shooting. This year, he's shooting it with much more confidence and rhythm, making 18 of his 34 attempts through his first five games. Simultaneously, he's continuing to do all the little things that made him so intriguing in the first place with his motor, physicality, rebounding, and defensive versatility.

Recent findings suggest that speaking of shooting, Braylon Mullins is establishing himself as one of the nation's premier shooters, as expected, despite the fact that he's clearly not 100% healthy. Through his first five games, he's made 19 threes on 50 attempts, but it's been the types of shots that have really stood out. He's running all over the court, flying off screens, and making threes on the move, all while being the focal point of opposing defenses. In short, Mullins is making the type of tough shots that translate to the next level, despite not having his typical ability to separate.

Sources indicate that one of the defining characteristics of the national 2026 recruiting class was the number of prospects who had glaring potential, but had yet to put it all together. That list included the likes of Duke's Cameron Williams,  Ohio State's Anthony Thompson, Maryland's Baba Oladotun, Christian Collins,  Adonis Rayliff and Darius Ratliff, all at USC. Nevertheless, almost all of them commanded the type of recruitment and correlating financial commitment that suggested programs were willing to invest in their development.

So far In t those investments have not resulted in the types of gains we had hoped for. The Ratliffs, Adonis in particular, have revealed some flashes, while Collins has only recently been cleared. Williams and Oladotun are barely in the rotation, and Thompson is playing, but not making the type of impact that anyone hoped.

Sources indicate that now, despite the lack of immediate return at the college level, most NBA decision-makers are still playing the long game, so I wouldn't expect any of these guys to be given up on just yet. Nevertheless, their early struggles did have to be accounted for on the massive board, which is why many of them are now outside the top 30.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After missing out on bigger name free agent starting pitchers like Tarik Skubal, Trevor Rogers, and Freddy Peralta, the Toronto Blue Jays have fortified their rotation by signing free agent right-hander Kaima Taira out of Japan. The deal is for $80 million over five years with an opt-out after the third year, the New York Post reports.

Earlier this offseason, CBS Sports ranked the undersized Taira as the No. 19 free agent of the current 2026-27 class. Here's part of that write-up:.

"Listed at 5-foot-8, Taira gets outlier extension down the mound (close to seven feet despite his height), which creates a low release window. Hitters rarely see the ball come from where Taira releases it. He's not a gimmick pitcher either. Taira sits mid-90s with his four-seam fastball and backs it up with a cutter, sinker, sweeper, slider, changeup, and splitter. The sweeper and slider are distinct pitches, as are the changeup and splitter. The Seibu Lions used Taira as a reliever in 2024 and 2025, then started him in 2026, and he handled the assignment well. The breaking balls are just OK, and the fact of the matter is that pitchers this height don't often hold up under a starter's workload. I would assume the team that signs Taira will give him a chance to start. In the long run, though, he might be a reliever, perhaps even a multi-inning setup man. Seibu declared on Oct. 30 that Taira will be posted this offseason.".

In a recent development, for his NPB career, Taira has a 1.85 ERA with 676 strikeouts in 633 ⅔ innings in a mix of rotation and bullpen duty. While, as noted above, Taira may not profile as a starter in MLB, the Jays will likely give him every opportunity to stick in their rotation, given their need there behind ace Dylan Cease. In addition to the $80 million commitment to Taira, the Jays will owe his former team, the Seibu Lions, a posting fee per the MLB-NPB agreement.

According to recent reports, toronto won the pennant in 2025 but backslid in 2026 to 83 losses and a last-place finish in the American League East. The offense was their leading liability last season, but the rotation also needed attention. That explains why they were very much in the bidding for Skubal and other premium starting pitchers on the market. It furthermore explains why they're willing to take a chance on Taira.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The road to the Super Bowl runs through the Buffalo Bills, who stand atop the AFC through 11 weeks and are poised to dominate their division en route to a potential first-round bye in the postseason. Most of the division leaders in this conference, Bills included, are runaway favorites, so the drama in the battle for the top four seeds should be limited over the final two months of the regular season. But the wild card race is a different story.

The bottom is falling out in the AFC in real time, leaving an uninspiring crop of teams vying for the final spots in the bracket. The Houston Texans stand two games below .500 but have just as strong a chance as practically any non-division leader of clinching a spot in the field. That goes to show how few competent squads exist outside of the top four.

It has been revealed that quarterback injuries are to blame for some of these woes, but the middle tier's struggles go beyond Drake Maye's fractured fibula and Lamar Jackson's thumb surgery. Three teams will rise from this group of wild card hopefuls nonetheless, earning spots in the seven-team bracket.

Here is a breakdown of the AFC playoff picture and a ranking of the seven strongest wild card contenders.

Division title and playoff odds via DraftKings Sportsbook.

It has been revealed that defense is an increasingly concerning matter for the Raiders. They rank 29th in EPA per play allowed and have surrendered at least 30 points in all but one game since Week 4. It is going to be nearly impossible to win games unless Fernando Mendoza quickly turns his promise into production as a prolific young quarterback. This offense, as currently constructed, is not built to put 30 or more points on the board every week.

According to recent reports, but signs in Mendoza's second start suggested the future is bright. He still took too many sacks and completed only 18 of 37 passes, but the No. 1 pick displayed real dual-threat playmaking ability in a three-touchdown effort against the Broncos. Ashton Jeanty even got off the schneid with a much-needed standout performance, breaking loose for a 46-yard run and scoring on the longest receiving play of his career: a 68-yarder. That Mendoza and Jeanty found so much success even without Brock Bowers in the lineup provides room for optimism.

The question is whether this will carry forward through the rest of the season or if it will take until 2027 and beyond for the offense to realize its potential. It at least has the makings of a unit that could win a game or two down the stretch.

In a recent development, by the time Lamar Jackson returns — if he comes back at all this season — it will be too late to salvage Year 1 of the Jesse Minter era. Six consecutive losses completely tanked what was once an exciting start to a latest coaching tenure. The Ravens would be hard-pressed to lose out since Jacoby Brissett has finally stabilized the offense a bit, but where will the wins come from as they work their way through a schedule that still features four games against divisional opponents in a surprisingly competitive AFC North?

It has been revealed that A bigger problem than the offense is the defense, which is a complete surprise given Minter's track record as a premier coach on that side of the ball. He was supposed to turn the group around with his acumen and the uptick in talent the franchise experienced over the offseason when it brought in Trey Hendrickson and retained stars in the secondary. Instead, his unit ranks 21st in DVOA and 18th in EPA per play allowed. Every opponent in the last five games, save the Chargers, scored at least 33 points against Minter's squad. And the Chargers won their matchup to get their first win of the season.

Slightly better days are ahead now that Derrick Henry is rolling again and the passing game is at least somewhat functional with Brissett under center. But the playoffs are probably out of reach.

The Patriots are difficult to handicap at this juncture because the quarterback shakeup hasn't had much time to marinate. The safe bet is to assume Tommy DeVito will not rebound much from the dismal showing he put up in Week 10, when he stepped in early in the loss to the Lions and led the team on just one scoring drive over the final three quarters. Considering the plethora of injuries elsewhere on the roster — most notably with A.J. Brown set to miss multiple weeks and the offensive line remaining a revolving door — New England lacks the weapons to make up for any bleak play from DeVito.

Drake Maye was essentially the only reason the Patriots still had life in the postseason hunt. At his best, he held together an injury-riddled roster and willed it to victories with performances that reflected his near-MVP-caliber play in 2025. But then there were the disastrous outings that indicated just how bad this team is when its quarterback is not pulling off heroics.

In a recent development, unfortunately for New England, it should expect more of the latter so long as DeVito is in the lineup. With Maye out indefinitely as he recovers from a fractured fibula, this season is headed down the drain.

Something is not quite right in Pittsburgh and now Aaron Rodgers has been benched for Mason Rudolph. Two weeks ago, the Steelers had the inside track to a top-four seed. Now they are on the outside of the playoffs looking in. The last two games were two of their worst all year and sounded every alarm.

The Steelers basically no-showed in a primetime divisional showdown with the Bengals two weeks ago and followed that embarrassing contest with a loss to the Eagles, who hadn't won a game in two months. In the process, DK Metcalf lost his composure and earned an ejection, the defense allowed Joe Burrow and Ja'Marr Chase to do whatever they wanted and a typically efficient run game reverted into a non-factor. Nothing went right.

Pittsburgh is at a crossroads. The vibes in the Steel City are sour, and unless this team gets itself right in short order, it could be in for a downward spiral. But at the same time, Mike McCarthy had his team looking like a surefire playoff contender through the first half of the campaign, so a return to form could lead to a trip to the postseason.

A thrilling comeback against the Texans ensured the Browns didn't hit their bye week on an extended skid, which could do wonders for team morale as they enter the stretch run. In erasing a 17-0 deficit and stunning Houston, the Browns put themselves in the driver's seat in the wild card race. With a manageable remaining schedule that offers plenty of winnable games outside of two contests against the Bengals, Cleveland could be in line to get into the dance for the first time since 2023 and just the fourth time this century.

According to recent reports, even if they come up short, Todd Monken deserves ample credit for making the Browns one of the NFL's most pleasant surprises of the year. The first-year coach inherited a roster hardly anyone believed in and turned it into a division contender, while making the Deshaun Watson contract look a little less disastrous and turning Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion into Rookie of the Year candidates. The defense is fairly solid even in a post-Myles Garrett world, too.

Ideally, Cleveland would jumpstart its run game when it returns from its off week and get Quinshon Judkins rolling, but with the young wide receiver corps performing and Watson playing above expectations, the Browns might be able to throw their way into the playoffs.

Sources indicate that the further removed the Texans become from their 0-4 start, the more baffling it becomes that they did, in fact, start the season winless. C.J. Stroud continues to play the best football of his career. Will Anderson Jr. is a top-tier Defensive Player of the Year candidate. The wide receiver group is deep and helped Houston field the seventh-best passing attack by yards per game over the first 11 weeks. Three of their last four wins came by 22 or 23 points. The full product of late is more in line with preseason expectations than with the disastrous start.

Recent findings suggest that at the same time, the defense outside of Anderson is a total disappointment, and the Texans cannot run the ball with any kind of consistency or explosiveness. Those deficiencies make the 4-6 record a little more comprehensible.

Industry observers note that the margin for error is extremely slim. Houston would become just the second team to bounce back from an 0-4 start and reach the postseason if it gets into the playoffs. But in a wild-card race where almost every other team has greater flaws than the Texans, this team has a realistic chance to climb above .500 for the first time this year and sneak into the No. 6 or No. 7 seed.

The Chiefs are a tiebreaker away from owning the No. 2 seed and avoiding the wild card picture altogether. At 8-2, Kansas City is battling the Broncos for the AFC West crown and only stands behind them because of the teams' win percentage against common opponents. Splitting the regular-season series with the Broncos reduces some of the Chiefs' control over their own destiny, but only in the hunt for a top-four seed—not on their path to a postseason berth. It would take a complete collapse for Andy Reid's crew to fall short of a spot in the bracket.

Industry observers note that the most favorable schedule in the league through 11 games helped the Chiefs turn themselves back into Super Bowl contenders after missing the playoffs a year ago, but to their credit, they have demolished overmatched opponents. It is not like they are simply skating by and leaning on a slate loaded with bottom-dwellers. Six of their eight wins have come by double-digit margins.

In a recent development, who are the Chiefs, really? The next five weeks will paint a clearer picture. Road games against the Bills, Rams and Bengals and a home clash with the 49ers are the kinds of tough tests they mostly avoided over the last three months.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Veteran right-handed starter Freddy Peralta has signed with the Baltimore Orioles on a five-year deal, the team unveiled on Tuesday. The contract is worth $125 million with no deferrals or options, The Athletic reports.

In a recent development, peralta, who will be going into his age-31 season in 2027, is coming off a campaign in which he didn't pitch up to his usual standards during a disastrous stint with the New York Mets. However, he did more like his old self following a deadline trade to the Tampa Bay Rays. On the Rays' watch, Peralta made a series of adjustments that helped him find better results on the mound, including being named the ALCS MVP.

According to recent reports, earlier this offseason, CBS Sports ranked Peralta as the No. 7 free agent of the 2026-27 class. Here's part of our write-up:.

In a recent development, "It has been a roller coaster year for Peralta, who flopped with the Mets, rebounded with the Rays, then faced the Brewers (his former team) in the World Series and lost. The post-deadline stint with Tampa salvaged Peralta's free agent year. They made several adjustments, most notably raising his arm angle and getting him to pitch exclusively from the stretch, and the result was a livelier fastball and also better command. He's still five-and-fly Freddy. Even the best version of Peralta won't pitch deep into games and can be a tough watch because he nibbles and throws so many pitches per inning. They tend to be good innings, though, and the guy never misses a start. Worst case, Peralta is a mid-rotation starter you can count on to take the ball every fifth day. The best case is someone who can front a contender's rotation. Fastball Freddy was always going to be a great bounceback candidate this offseason. The Rays just beat everyone to it at the trade deadline.".

Peralta isn't far removed from a 2023-25 stretch for the Milwaukee Brewers that saw him top 30 starts and 200 strikeouts in three straight seasons. In 2025, he earned his second All-Star selection and finished fifth in the National League Cy Young vote.

According to recent reports, "Freddy has proven to be a winning player who understands what it takes to compete and succeed on the biggest stage," remarked Orioles president of baseball operations Mike Elias said in a statement. "His professionalism, preparation, and commitment to winning will set a strong example for our organization and we believe he will have a significant impact on our team both on and off the field.".

Industry observers note that after losing Trevor Rogers to free agency (he agreed to a five-year contract with the Chicago Cubs earlier on Tuesday), the Orioles were searching for a upcoming frontline starter to join a rotation that includes Kyle Bradish, Shane Baz and some combination of Brandon Young, Cade Povich and Trey Gibson. Elias has been hesitant to pay up for pitchers recently, but either his strategy has changed or he decided Peralta was worth the cost.

The Orioles' disappointing fourth-place AL East finish in 2026 has raised questions about the state of Baltimore's rebuild, particularly amid stalled growth from its promising young position players, including Jackson Holliday, Gunnar Henderson and Colton Cowser. Would-be franchise backstop Adley Rutschman was traded to the Boston Red Sox at the trade deadline.

Because Peralta was traded during the 2026 season and was thus ineligible for the qualifying offer, the Orioles will not be penalized a draft pick for signing him.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • We're now a month into the 2026-27 NBA season, and while we're still weeks away from the unofficial start of trade season (Dec.
  • According to recent reports, firm rumors are still in short supply, but we're at least getting some early buzz on who intends to do what in the months to come.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We're now a month into the 2026-27 NBA season, and while we're still weeks away from the unofficial start of trade season (Dec. 15), we've seen enough basketball for teams to at least begin making plans for the upcoming transaction cycle. Teams are starting to know how good they are, what sort of holes they're dealing with and what the market is going to look like as we draw closer to the February trade deadline.

According to recent reports, firm rumors are still in short supply, but we're at least getting some early buzz on who intends to do what in the months to come. So let's check in on what has made the rounds lately.

Sources indicate that the 14-3 Los Angeles Lakers are headed for a titanic clash with the San Antonio Spurs on Friday that will presumably put one of those two teams in pole position in the Western Conference. Last Friday, however, head of basketball operations Rob Pelinka did a pregame interview with Spectrum SportsNet in which he made it clear he looks to be aggressive ahead of February's deadline.

Sources indicate that "We'll be active at the trade deadline to shore up things that we see," Pelinka said. "We think this team has a real chance to make a run, so we want to give the group as much talent as we can. Don't want to get too far over our skis with a hot start, because you don't want to get substantial-headed, but clearly the way it's gone so far, it's been great and we hope it continues.".

Industry observers note that the Lakers are very limited in terms of tradable draft capital because of their significant July swing for Walker Kessler. They only have one first-round asset available, and it's only swap rights in 2032. They picked up two useful second-round picks in the Deandre Ayton trade, though, giving them three in total. That's not enough for a blockbuster, but it's helpful liquidity. Further, the Lakers are relatively financially flexible going into the deadline as well. They're barely over the luxury-tax line and have around $8 million in room beneath their first apron hard cap, allowing them to potentially make a somewhat unbalanced trade if the need presents itself.

So, what would the Lakers be looking for at the deadline? Two obvious needs stand out:.

As Marc Stein noted, the Los Angeles Clippers have moved to a veteran-only starting lineup, with Darius Garland, Rui Hachimura, Derrick Jones Jr., Max Strus and Brook Lopez opening games lately. Brandon Ingram, returning Monday, is sure to join that group, and Kris Dunn is a central part of their rotation. All of these players but Ingram and Garland are on expiring deals, and Stein noted that the Clippers are "regarded as a certain seller" ahead of the trade deadline.

It has been revealed that and, well, that makes plenty of sense. The Clippers were just stripped of five first-round picks in the Kawhi Leonard scandal. Those expiring contracts belong to players who almost certainly won't be a part of the next great Clipper team, but they could help replenish the team's draft capital moving forward.

Industry observers note that the Clippers are, by far, the most versatile seller on the market right now. In theory, they could burnish just about any contender. Need defense? Jones and Dunn have you covered. Offense? Strus and Hachimura are proven playoff snipers. The center market is in the middle of a supply-demand crisis. Lopez has been sensational this season and could give any contender a solid 20 minutes per night. With Keaton Wagler in the building, it's hard to imagine they'd even shut the door on a good enough Garland offer. Expect the Clippers to live in the rumor mill for the next few months. They have several players who could legitimately impact the championship hunt.

Recent findings suggest that last week, SNY dropped a stunner of a rumor: that the Utah Jazz, loaded with young guards and off to a terrible start, had had internal conversations about pursuing Mavericks guard Kyrie Irving. The rumor didn't make much sense in the moment, and The Salt Lake Tribune reported Monday that the Jazz "don't appear to have any real interest" in the future Hall of Famer.

They have, however, talked trade with the team we just discussed: the Clippers. Those conversations began with "various Clippers bigs" and have moved on to wing depth, of which the Clippers have plenty. The Jazz are reportedly casting a wide net in pursuit of help.

The 3-15 Jazz have been among the NBA's biggest disappointments this season. A lot of that has been the result of injuries, with Jaren Jackson Jr. and Lauri Markkanen out now and Jusuf Nurkić having not yet debuted this season. The Jazz are painfully thin in the front court at this point, and the early partnership between Keyonte George and Darryn Peterson in the backcourt has yielded mixed results.

Casting a wide net makes sense since the Jazz could theoretically use help basically anywhere. More of a playmaking guard to balance out the score-first instincts that George and Peterson bring would make sense. Wing depth, especially defense-first wing depth, would help address a major weakness. Dunn is a former Jazz player. And of course, adding some size to deal with all of those injuries would probably have the biggest immediate impact. Utah doesn't control its own first-round pick this year. The Jazz benefit from losing in no way, and that has seemingly made them eager to try to fight an uphill battle back into the Western Conference Play-In race.

Celtic manager Martin O’Neill hailed midfield duo Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain and Luke McCowan after the recalled pair both scored in the 4-1 home win over St Mirren.

With Mika Baur facing 10 weeks out with an ankle injury and Benjamin Nygren nursing a heel problem, O’Neill handed McCowan his second start of the season and Oxlade-Chamberlain his fifth, as the two joined forces for the first time.

Oxlade-Chamberlain and McCowan netted either side of Camilo Duran in a nine-minute flurry of goals late in the first half with Callum McGregor making it four for Celtic in the second period before Killian Phillips reduced the deficit for Saints from the penalty spot.

Recent findings suggest that O’Neill noted: ‘Alex has been waiting around for a while to get into the side. He’s a brilliant passer of the ball. He took his goal very well with a calm finish in the bottom corner.

‘He was feeling a little bit sore, so taking him off was just precautionary.

In a recent development, ‘I was also delighted Luke got his goal. That should give him a boost in confidence.’.

Oxlade-Chamberlain congratulates McCowan after he scored to make it three for Celtic.

McCowan faced criticism after Celtic’s Champions League collapse against LASK and his only previous start this season saw him taken off at half-time in a home defeat by Rangers.

O’Neill remarked: ‘I thought he did really well, also playing the full game given it has been some considerable time since he has done that.

In a recent development, ‘He got the ball early on and played it almost blindly and it was intercepted and I thought, “oh, gosh, here we go”. But he roared back, took his goal well and I am really pleased for him. He is a real genuine lad.

It has been revealed that ‘It has been tough for him. In the game against Rangers, he was thrown into a position, and it didn’t start well for him in the match. I think he felt it was deja vu for him in terms of the game at the back end of last season too. That will be good for him.’.

The Celtic manager also introduced 19-year-old former PSV Eindhoven midfielder Joel van den Berg for a debut in the second half.

In a recent development, ‘I thought he did very well,’ stated O’Neill. ‘He’s coming on after an injury which kept him out for some time.

‘I am pleased there is a bit of competition for places now.’.

The veteran midfielder celebrates his strike that opened the scoring against St Mirren.

St Mirren manager Craig McLeish felt Celtic were clinical in his team’s heavy defeat in Glasgow.

‘It’s a really sore one with the way the scoreline ended up,’ said McLeish.

According to recent reports, ‘I thought we started the game quite well and then that flurry of goals can happen here when you’re playing against such a strong team. The difference was the quality in our box compared to theirs.

‘They are just so clinical, and they get into those good areas and they punish you.

In a recent development, ‘I felt we got into some similar areas throughout the game. We didn’t give up, we didn’t move away from what we were trying to do, but we were just really lacking that final bit.’.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that the uncertain 2026-27 Major League Baseball offseason is fully underway.
  • Thanks to that prospect of a hastened pace, offseason rumors are flowing.
  • Free agent catcher Tyler Stephenson has agreed to a three-year contract to return to the Reds, reports ESPN.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the uncertain 2026-27 Major League Baseball offseason is fully underway. The ongoing CBA negotiations and the near certainty of an owner-implemented lockout on Dec. 2 loom over all, and it may indeed mean a flurry of trades and free agent signings leading up to that date. That was certainly the case leading up to the last lockout of 2021-22, and this time around we've already seen some leading examples. Just recently, for instance, the New York Mets landed the biggest fish in the pond by signing ace Tarik Skubal to a record contract. Not long after, the Chicago Cubs fortified their rotation with Trevor Rogers and their outfield with Teruaki Sato, and Freddy Peralta is headed to the Baltimore Orioles. More's surely to come before lockout day arrives.

Thanks to that prospect of a hastened pace, offseason rumors are flowing. Speaking of which, we'll be here each day to round up what's out there. You can find Tuesday's supply just below.

Free agent catcher Tyler Stephenson has agreed to a three-year contract to return to the Reds, reports ESPN. The deal is worth $30 million and includes an opt-out after the second year. Cincinnati selected Stephenson, 30, with the No. 11 pick in the 2015 draft, and he's played his entire career with the Reds. We ranked him as the 46th-best free agent available.

The Reds will again pair Stephenson with glove-first backup Jose Trevino behind the plate. Cincinnati now figures to turn their attention to the pitching staff, both the rotation and bullpen. Hunter Greene's UCL surgery means Andrew Abbott and Chase Burns are the only locks for the rotation, though Nick Lodolo will have a spot as long as he's healthy.

In a recent development, the Yankees are among the many teams with interest in top free agent reliever Adrian Morejon, reports the Latest York Post. Some teams view him as a potential starter, though there were reports earlier this month that he prefers to stay in the bullpen. The Phillies, meanwhile, are not considered a serious candidate to sign Morejon, according to The Athletic. We ranked him as the second-best free agent available this offseason, in part due to his potential to start.

According to recent reports, adding to the bullpen has been the Yankees' primary focus so far this offseason. Closer David Bednar accepted the qualifying offer, they re-signed lefty matchup guy Tim Hill, and signed Jonathan Loáisiga and Tim Hill as free agents. At some point they will need to add to their lineup, particularly at third base, but there's always room for a reliever like Morejon in the bullpen.

According to recent reports, the Philadelphia Phillies are open to moving Trea Turner off of shortstop given that he's now a pronounced defensive liability. Speaking of openness, veteran shortstop Corey Seager of the Texas Rangers is willing to waive his no-trade clause to join the Phillies and upgrade the position for them, NBC Sports Philadelphia reports.

Recent findings suggest that now 32, Seager will always have health and durability concerns, but he remains a plus defensive shortstop who produces well at the plate by positional standards. Signed to a 10-year, $325 million deal prior to the 2022 season (just before the last lockout, in fact), Seager is owed another $155 million through the 2031 season. The Rangers are reportedly looking to shake things up. The Phillies, meantime, are trying to keep their contention window open. It's a fit both ways, at least in theory. Such a move would likely mean a move to the outfield for Turner, who himself has very little trade value thanks to his ongoing decline and massive contract.

Industry observers note that even in a down 2026 year, Jazz Chisholm Jr. put up 19 homers and stole 41 bases while manning an up-the-middle position. Still just 28 years of age, he figures to have a healthy market this offseason. Speaking of which, the Washington Nationals are one of multiple teams presently in contact with Chisholm, FanSided reports.

Earlier in the offseason, CBS Sports ranked Chisholm as the No. 6 free agent in the current class. Here's part of that write-up:.

"In what was his worst season as a hitter since his rookie year in 2021, Chisholm was still a league-average bat in 2026, and his top-shelf defense and baserunning still landed him at 3.5 WAR. Chisholm is a style-over-substance player who is not for everyone, but his second base defense and near-MLB-best baserunning skills give him a very high floor. He's a reasonable bet for 20-ish home runs with the potential to go 30-30, and Chisholm has improved his plate discipline enough to run walk rates north of 10% the last two years. The downside is his propensity to swing and miss. Chisholm has posted below-average in-zone contact rates throughout his career and contact rates that low always come with risk. That risk is mitigated somewhat by the secondary skills (defense, etc.) and the fact that Chisholm will play the entire 2027 season at age 29. You probably don't want him as your best or second-best player, but he's also an overqualified No. 6-7 hitter who brings so much else to the table.".

The Cleveland Guardians have agreed to a free-agent contract with left-hander Kris Bubic, Sportsnet reports. The contract is for $17.5 million over one year, according to ESPN. Bubic, 29, made nine starts for the Kansas City Royals last season, and after the trade to the Los Angeles Dodgers, he was used out of the bullpen. Bubic has an outlier fastball thanks to its rise and his unusual release point, and he's an interesting "ceiling" candidate in the rotation. However, his substantial history of injuries may mean he's best used out of the bullpen.

The Detroit Tigers have added infield depth by agreeing to terms with Ha-Seong Kim on a one-year, $5 million free agent contract, ESPN reports. Kim, 31, is coming off a rough partial season with the Atlanta Braves, but he has a more palatable OPS+ of 91 for his career. He's been a primary shortstop in recent years and also has significant time spent at second base and third base.

Sources indicate that even after achieving a reunion with veteran starting pitcher Sonny Gray, the Minnesota Twins are still looking to fortify their roster for a return to contention in 2027. The club still hopes to make one more significant addition this offseason and add another player who may not grab as many headlines, the Athletic reports. Atop the wishlist are a first baseman or a second baseman and another lefty reliever.

Even after the splash addition of Skubal, the Mets may not be done adding starting pitchers in the service of a rebound season in 2027. On that front, the Mets may be interested in adding a starting pitcher on a short-term deal for next season, the Athletic reports. That would likely limit them to the back half of the market, especially with so many bigger names reaching agreements.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The only thing that pairs better with football than Thanksgiving is betting on football. Fortunately for us, we don't have to compromise this week, as the NFL is locked and loaded with tons of action over the holiday weekend. We are about to embark on a marathon that has five days of games over a six-day stretch.

It has been revealed that this is why we put in the work over the offseason and stay in tip-top betting shape. It's so that when we reach pockets like this where the games are coming in one after another, we have the stamina (and bankroll) to keep up.

This barrage of games comes at a swell time for us in this little betting corner of the internet, as I'm heading into this stretch with a strong record over the last month or so. Week 11 was a more modest outcome, but our heads were above water. I was 9-4 straight-up and 7-6 against the spread for the entire slate and went 3-2 ATS on my five locks of the week. That brings me to a 35-7 straight-up mark and a 10-5 ATS record with my locks over the last three weeks. That's certainly something to be thankful for, and I'll look to keep it rolling as we step toward Week 12.

All lines via DraftKings; All times ET.

According to recent reports, I get that Chicago is riding a five-game winning streak into this Thanksgiving matchup and that they've looked like a bona fide Super Bowl threat after acquiring Jeffery Simmons. That said, I think the Lions are getting disrespected a bit with this line making them a home dog.

Detroit has largely owned the Bears as of late, sweeping them in each of the last two seasons. Over that stretch, Jared Goff has averaged 305.5 passing yards per game and has 11 touchdowns with just one interception. Jahmyr Gibbs has reached at least 100 scrimmage yards in all four of those games as well.

While that history is nice to lean on, the true reason I like taking the home dog in this matchup is their defense. Sure, Simmons will get a lot of shine for his impact on Chicago, but Brian Branch has also helped change the fortunes of Detroit's unit. Since Branch has returned to the secondary, the Lions are 5-0 and allowing 14.4 points per game. Their 248.6 yards per game allowed and 168.6 passing yards per game allowed are both top five in the NFL over that span.

Projected score: Lions 27, Bears 23The pick: Lions +2.5.

Recent findings suggest that thursday's Thanksgiving finale will mark the 11th time that Patrick Mahomes and Josh Allen have squared off against one another in their careers. On the whole, this rivalry has been one-sided depending on the time of year. In the regular season, Allen is 5-1 against Mahomes, but the Chiefs quarterback is a perfect 4-0 in the playoffs. Seeing as this is a regular-season matchup, one would think this trend could continue, especially with the Bills playing at Highmark Stadium. However, I think Mahomes gets a rare regular-season win over his rival.

Mahomes comes into Week 12 with his hair on fire, totaling 13 touchdowns and zero interceptions over his last four games. Not only do those numbers bolster his sure-fire Comeback Player of the Year candidacy, but they're making him a dark-horse MVP candidate. Buffalo's defense has put up some eye-popping numbers as they've gone three straight games without allowing a touchdown. However, these are the quarterbacks they've faced over that stretch: Carson Wentz, Max Brosmer, Geno Smith, Cade Klubnik, and Kyle McCord. Mahomes is in another stratosphere.

Meanwhile, Kansas City's defense has been sneaky great this year, owning the best red zone scoring efficiency (36%) in the league entering Week 12.

Projected score: Chiefs 28, Bills 24The pick: Chiefs +3.

Industry observers note that I've already covered the fact that Pittsburgh firmly has its back against the wall — and rather extensively — this week. They're 0-2 since coming out of their bye week and have seen their playoff position start to slip, falling from the No. 6 seed to the No. 7 seed last weekend. This is, in part, why I'm taking them to pull off the upset at home over the Broncos. They're simply the more desperate team. If they don't win here, it could be the beginning of the end to their season.

Sources indicate that if they lose, they run the risk of falling out of the playoff picture entirely and set up another do-or-die matchup with the Texans in Week 13. Playing at home, this is a gotta-have-it moment for Mike McCarthy and Aaron Rodgers.

It has been revealed that fortunately for them, they do matchup pretty well against Denver. While their ground game has been one of the main reasons for their struggles over the past two weeks, it has a strong opportunity to get back on track this Friday. The Broncos are allowing 4.6 yards per carry this season, which is tied for the fifth-highest in the NFL. During Sunday's win over the Raiders, Denver allowed Ashton Jeanty to post 169 yards from scrimmage. Jaylen Warren has the ability to make that same type of impact as both a receiver and runner out of the backfield.

Moreover, the Steelers' run defense should be able to contain what has blossomed into a strong Broncos ground attack headlined by Jonah Coleman. Pittsburgh's 3.6 yards per carry allowed average this season is tied for the second-fewest in the league. The defense has also allowed the seventh-fewest points per game (20.1). If they can bottle up Coleman and put more emphasis on Bo Nix, that could be the winning formula.

Projected score: Steelers 23, Broncos 20The pick: Steelers +3.

According to recent reports, the Vikings are likely frustrated with how their Week 11 loss to the 49ers went down in Mexico City. While the 35-10 final score looks lopsided, Minnesota had self-inflicted wounds, including a pick-six by Kirk Cousins and a brutal fumble by Justin Jefferson at the start of the second half. They have a great opportunity to get back on track when they return home and host a Falcons team that is nowhere close to the caliber of San Francisco.

In a recent development, we all know that Brian Flores deploys blitzes like no other coordinator in the NFL. While Brock Purdy sliced it up last Sunday in Mexico City, Michael Penix ranks 27th out of 32 quarterbacks in EPA per dropback when blitzed this season, according to TruMedia.

Sources indicate that meanwhile, the Falcons defense is allowing touchdowns on 67.6% of red zone trips this season, the sixth-highest rate in the NFL. That should result in Cousins having much easier sledding against his former team. This is as ripe a bounce-back spot as you'll find.

Projected score: Vikings 27, Falcons 17The pick: Vikings -7.

This is a bad spot for the Ravens, who can't seem to catch a break this season. Baltimore is right now on a six-game losing streak, coinciding with Lamar Jackson's injury. They also have a historically poor defense and now have to go on the road to face a Texans team that possesses the rest advantage after playing last Thursday. That's a recipe for this losing skid to continue.

According to recent reports, the Ravens' defense ranks 26th in scoring this season, and their 26.7 points per game allowed is on pace to be the second-most in team history. They've also allowed 30 or more points in four of the last five games.

That's music to C.J. Stroud's ears, as the Texans quarterback has completely revitalized himself in 2026 and reestablished himself as one of the top signal-callers in the league. Stroud is currently tied with Mahomes for the best TD-INT ratio in the NFL. He's also top seven in the league in passing yards and passing touchdowns. Stroud has thrown at least three touchdowns in three straight games entering Week 12.

Getting this line under a touchdown is an auto-bet, considering how Stroud and the Ravens defense are playing right now.

Man City survive tunnel clash and Porto fury thanks to Haaland double

⏱️ ~26 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Erling Haaland revealed on the eve of this clash how he loves chopping firewood in his spare time – and his goals set alight Manchester City’s Champions League campaign on a fractious evening in Porto.
  • Sources indicate that so much for the new group stage of the competition taking time to warm up.
  • And City were not easing themselves back into European action either, they went full throttle at the start of a tough set of group games.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Erling Haaland revealed on the eve of this clash how he loves chopping firewood in his spare time – and his goals set alight Manchester City’s Champions League campaign on a fractious evening in Porto.

Sources indicate that so much for the new group stage of the competition taking time to warm up. This clash was a hot-blooded, bitter contest that spilt over in the tunnel at half-time, with players getting separated and tempers rising.

And City were not easing themselves back into European action either, they went full throttle at the start of a tough set of group games. With Enzo Maresca, it looks like it will be all-out attack to get the best out of this team.

They can look nervous at the back, particularly with the ball at Gianluigi Donnarumma’s feet, but have attacking weapons to hurt any team in this elite competition. This was a performance that their rivals will take note of.

“It was a complete performance on and off the ball for 95 minutes,” was Maresca’s assessment.

According to recent reports, city will certainly scare the traditional heavyweights with Haaland leading their attack and taking an axe to Porto’s defence like he does with logs in his back garden. It was his 58th and 59th goal in 59 games in the Champions League, with his latest an expertly directed header off a post and a calm side-footed finish.

NO MISTAKE from Erling Haaland this time 💪He's put Man City 1-0 up in Porto 🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/UpKOqQA49s.

There is an argument that Pep Guardiola could have achieved more in the Champions League, given City’s dominance in domestic football. They have been knocked out by Real Madrid in the last three seasons but this is a new City, different personnel and even a new look.

They wore their black and yellow away kit, inspired by “Manchester’s iconic worker bee” according to Puma, and grafted their way to victory here. Non-stop running going forward, and scrapping with Porto, too.

Recent findings suggest that the Portuguese champions were not happy with Marc Guéhi’s challenge on Gabri Veiga and claimed an elbow was used, with the row carrying on in the tunnel at half-time with security guards separating the players. Rúben Dias also appeared to nudge a Porto official on his way to the dressing room.

“I didn’t see anything but anyway, you can ask how many times you see me or my bench stand up? Zero, for 95 minutes. How many times do you see their bench? So...” Maresca added.

Only Dias and Haaland remain from the starting line-up from the Champions League triumph three years ago, so this is essentially a newly introduced team with a new manager.

Erling Haaland seals the deal in Porto 🤝🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/10xSTtZ8nw.

Phil Foden, on as a sub in that game, started at Estádio do Dragão after his horse Wreck It Ronnie defeated Najidi Storm, which started the Goodwood race with 1-33 odds and is now the shortest-priced loser in British racing history. The rest of the team are latest to City’s challenge.

That includes Ayyoub Bouaddi, 18, who was part of a £320m midfield refresh following the departure of Rodri, who was named among the Ballon d’Or nominees a few hours before kick-off to highlight the experience and class City have lost.

It has been revealed that bouaddi, who cost £81.4m from Lille, made a good start in his full debut. The Moroccan teenager is neat on the ball and gets around the pitch, with the next step being able to dominate games like his predecessor.

Industry observers note that “In his last game he lost two balls and stayed calm and was back in our box,” Maresca said. “This shows how good he is because any player after two [poor] passes panics, but he is just 18. Erling, Rúben, Mateo [Kovacic], they can manage these kind of games better, but you don’t expect it from a guy of 18. I didn’t see him panic.”.

Sources indicate that by Bouaddi’s side in midfield was Enzo Fernández, who sought to drive forward into space when City counter-attacked. He was among the players who, along with Dias, were reminded of their Benfica history by the home fans.

Diogo Costa tends to be linked with a move to the Premier League every summer, but has been a one-club man for his career so far. But he showed why clubs are looking at him with his first-half saves to deny Haaland and Rayan Cherki.

Porto’s legendary goalkeeper, Helton, was in the press box at half-time and would have been impressed with the saves, although he was not in his seat when Haaland scored the first goal, which came 94 seconds after the restart.

Recent findings suggest that city had worked the ball around the penalty area, with Antoine Semenyo drawing out Costa before laying off to Fernández. Haaland’s header from the cross had such precision that the goalkeeper did not dive as it angled in off a post.

Still, Porto had their chances with Alberto Costa heading wide from a corner and William Gomes charging down a Donnarumma kick – with City’s most nervous moments coming when they passed around their back line.

In a recent development, man City are living dangerously here! 🫣Donnarumma nearly gifts Porto an equaliser 😬 pic.twitter.com/otIfZTHmdn.

But Haaland sealed the win as the game ticked into stoppage time, finding the bottom corner from Rayan Aït-Nouri’s cutback.

“It was an amazing game against the champions of Portugal. We knew it would be a difficult fight, man against man, they are a top team,” Haaland mentioned. “They play amazing football. All the pressure, we have to deliver on the significant stage and that’s what we did. We controlled the whole first half, created chances.”.

For Maresca, the victory was also a challenge against Porto’s aggression, with the Italian coach adding: “I was very pleased. We know in this kind of game when you come here it’s always difficult or tricky. The environment, the way they grew up, it’s normal, but I think we dealt with that very good.”.

Top performance, Enzo 👊✨ pic.twitter.com/ds0f207tpS.

It has been a positive start for Unai Emery’s Aston Villa out in Belgium as they lead Club Brugge 3-1 at half-time.

Enzo Maresca takes charge of his first Champions League game in charge of Manchester City as they have travelled to Portugal to take on Porto at the Estadio do Dragao. These sides last met during the Champions League group stages during the 2020/21 season. Manchester City won 3-1 at home before the two sides drew 0-0 in this stadium.

Industry observers note that manchester City were busy late on in the transfer window, bringing in both Iliman Ndiaye and Enzo Fernandez as they spent nearly £200m on deadline day alone. They come into tonight’s game off the back of three straight Premier League victories to kick off the Maresca era. Maresca has limited Champions League experience as a manager, which came with Chelsea last season. Manchester City have won their opening game of a Champions League campaign in six of the last seven seasons but this will be the first time since 2015/16 that Manchester City embark on a Champions League campaign without Pep Guardiola at the helm.

“It is a hard place to come [Porto],” stated Maresca. “They have started really well. In the last 14/15 games in Europe they lost just one, that highlights a difficult place to come, but we will try our best and try to win the game. It is a very, very good team. They have different players, but in terms of the team it is very clear in the way they play. They are aggressive without the ball and on the ball, they have a clear style. But we will try our best and try to win the game. The ambition is the same; try to be ourselves and to win games and then we will see.”.

Porto, managed by Francesco Farioli, have won every league game so far this season and already sit four points clear at the summit of Liga Portugal. Farioli takes charge of his first game as a manger in the Champions League and the club make their return to the elite European competition after two seasons away.

According to recent reports, “We are going to face one of the massive favourites to win the competition,” Farioli noted. “It will be a game that will demand that we be at our best, and we know that whenever we step onto the Dragão pitch, something special can happen. I am happy to be in the Champions League for the first time at 37 years old. This will be my first game, but we approach every game with the same attention to detail and the same focus. It is easy for the players to be motivated tomorrow [tonight]. But the key will be our strategy and our ability to execute it, individually and collectively.”.

Porto were in the Europa League last season, making it to the quarter-finals, where they were knocked out by Nottingham Forest 2-1 on aggregate. The omens would not appear to be on Porto’s side tonight; they have only won two of their last 16 games against English opposition in major European competition.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that blake Griffin told an interesting story recently, recalling playing golf with former teammate JJ Redick. At that point, Redick was already retired and Griffin was nearing the end of his career.

It has been revealed that this was before Redick became the head coach of the Lakers. He had some perspective on his post-playing days that he offered to Griffin, something that stuck with the longtime Clipper years later. Redick told Griffin that he wouldn't be "truly happy" until he retired. Knowing how that might sound, Griffin was quick to clarify that they weren't miserable playing basketball, but rather that the two men were similar in their extensive, obsessive preparation.

"The way I took it and the way I think that he meant it," Griffin told GQ, "is it's such a grind, mental grind, physical grind of putting literally everything you have into this thing. And then when you're done, you just find this new sense of peace.".

Put another way, pressure is baked into being in the NBA. The severity might vary from player to player or team to team, but it's natural enough to feel a certain amount of weight given the intensity of the competition. With that in mind, here are some estimations on current stress levels around the league.

All things considered, the Sixers have to be pretty happy with how they've started the season. Even after the Blazers snapped their five-game win streak on Monday, Philly is 14-4 and sits atop the East. LeBron James, unsurprisingly, has been a fantastic addition, particularly as a distributor and playmaker. Jaylen Brown is playing his usual heavy minutes while shooting nearly 50% from the floor. And, crucially, Joel Embiid — who missed a combined 150 games over the previous three seasons — has appeared in all but four games to date. Those are all wins for the Sixers.

Industry observers note that to the extent that there's any cause for concern here, it's how sustainable all this is for them. Of the 18 games they've played, they're a perfect 12-0 in the clutch (games decided by five points or fewer with five minutes or less to go). That's tops in the NBA, and they must feel good about being at their best when things get a little dicey. But as Tyrese Maxey pointed out earlier in the season when they were starting to fall into this rhythm of playing close game after close game, he and the Sixers would prefer to stack a few victories that don't cause them to sweat right until the end.

Recent findings suggest that winning in the clutch sure beats the alternative. For now, it's less of a problem than something to monitor.

It has been revealed that just a couple of weeks ago, the Celtics won the battle of frenemies and were perched atop the Eastern Conference. Things haven't gone quite to plan since then. All of a sudden, the Celtics have lost four in a row, including two one-point losses at Sacramento and Golden State. Boston handed the Kings just their second win of the season, and dropped the game to the Stephen Curry-less Warriors. Not the kind of basketball the Celtics are accustomed to playing.

Things haven't been easy lately for Boston. The Sacramento and Golden State games were on a back-to-back as part of a difficult, still-in-progress stretch in the schedule in which Boston plays six of seven on the road, culminating in another back-to-back when the Celtics face the Spurs in San Antonio this coming Sunday, followed by the Mavericks in Dallas on Monday.

Sources indicate that perhaps most troubling of all, two-way star Derrick White has been merely a one-way contributor for a while now. White had a disappointing shooting season a year ago. Considering his talent, the smart bet was that he would bounce back and be more efficient this season. That hasn't happened. White is shooting 41% from the floor and an abysmal 28.9% from deep. The 3-point mark is the worst of his career by a good stretch. He made just 2 of 12 from distance against the Warriors and was visibly frustrated with himself.

In a recent development, the Celtics have long had a theory of how they like to play: take and make more 3s than the opposition on any given night. When their shots are falling, they're tough to beat. When they aren't, anyone can knock them off. Right now, they're struggling, White in particular. Boston doesn't really have any choice but to let White try to shoot his way back into form. He's too important to their overall looks, and they'd never be able to replace his impact at the other end of the floor, where he remains one of the best all-around defenders in the league. Either he fixes his shot and Boston is back in business, or he doesn't and life at the office gets a lot tougher for everyone.

In a recent development, when the Timberwolves declared in October that Anthony Edwards would undergo an arthroscopic procedure on his right knee, it took some people by surprise. Edwards looked good to start the season. He torched the Heat in the opening outing, going for 45 points and draining nine 3s. In his fourth game, on the second night of a back-to-back, he put up 47 points in a close two-point loss at Cleveland — and then suddenly and without warning, he was out of commission and expected to miss approximately two months.

Edwards recently mentioned that he "never wanted to have surgery" and he felt pretty good during the offseason. He thought he was managing the knee well then, and it wasn't swollen during the summer. But after the aforementioned back-to-back, the knee "was really bad, like painful to fly. So I'm like, 'I'm gonna get [the surgery].'".

Without him, the Wolves have fared better than some might have expected, going a tidy 10-4. They're third in the Western Conference, trailing only the Spurs and Lakers. That should have head coach Chris Finch and the Wolves optimistic about staying afloat until Edwards returns. Except no one seems to be sure when that might be, including Edwards, who recently cast some doubt on the initial timetable when he said he has "no clue" when he'll be back on the floor.

It has been revealed that if we go by the original estimation, two months would put Ant in late December. Now that ballpark appears far less than certain. The Wolves have performed admirably with him sidelined, but in a loaded West, Minnesota will need Edwards back sooner than "no clue" if it wants to stay near the top of the conference and especially if the Wolves hope to make a deep postseason run.

Industry observers note that ant is the unquestionable leader in all departments for Minnesota. In his absence, things have sometimes felt a little tense  — to the point where one noted knucklehead has periodically gotten frustrated by another. Getting Edwards back would definitely help on the court. It wouldn't hurt the vibes, either.

It has been revealed that what are the Cavs even doing? They're 9-9 after losing to the Bulls (without Caleb Wilson, no less) on Monday. That puts them one game up on the Magic for seventh in the East. They're just 2-6 outside of Cleveland. But hey, James Harden recently went for 51 points against the Pacers and now has more 50-point games in his career than Kobe Bryant. Maybe that will console Cavs fans. Seems unlikely, though.

In a recent development, when you reach the conference finals, bring back your four most important players and add a fifth starter coming off a promising season, the expectations are understandably high. So far, the Cavs haven't exactly met them. Cleveland has been a top 10 offensive team, but bottom 10 in defense. That leaves them pretty much looking like what their record indicates — average at best, a team that could lose to an inferior opponent (like, say, Chicago) on any random night in November.

In a recent development, it certainly hasn't helped that they've been without Evan Mobley of late. He's missed the last six games with a toe injury. Peyton Watson, the aforementioned addition to the starting lineup, hasn't been anywhere near as good in Cleveland as he was in Denver last season. All of that has left Donovan Mitchell with too much heavy lifting, and so far he hasn't been able to shoulder the load on his own. The longer this mediocrity continues, the more we're left to wonder whether the Cavs are overdue to shake up their starting unit and offload one of the significant names.

[Looks around to see if anyone else is cringing] They just lost to the Pacers.

In fairness, no team has been hit with more major injuries than the Thunder. Jalen Williams (leg) and Cason Wallace (shoulder) could very well miss the remainder of the season after both underwent surgery, while Chet Holmgren (knee) is expected to miss at least three months. That's three of the team's five starters to begin the season. Not good. Except to hear the reigning back-to-back MVP tell it, there's something unexpected to be gleaned from the experience.

"Honestly speaking, it's kind of fun," Shai Gilgeous-Alexander stated last week. "We've kind of had the wind at our back the last couple of years and had our way a lot of nights, and to have that kind of adversity, it's kind of fun. I embrace it. It'll make me better.".

Industry observers note that SGA has a different definition of fun than most people. After losing in Indiana on Monday, the Thunder are just two games over .500, which puts them 10th in the West. [Go ahead and cringe if you weren't already doing so.].

It has been revealed that if there's any team that can withstand SGA's bizarre version of a good time, it's the Thunder. Sam Presti assembled the deepest team in the NBA, but there are limits to what even they can handle. In the absence of several key players, Ajay Mitchell, Jared McCain, Isaiah Hartenstein and others have all been tasked with picking up considerable slack. That includes rookies Aday Mara and Bennett Stirtz. When you're missing so many vital pieces, you stop being deep at some point and just do your best to plug holes. Even the mighty Thunder can only do so much.

The Warriors snapped a five-game losing streak by beating the Celtics at home on Sunday in a white-knuckled one-point win. Alas, they only managed 88 points in the victory and the offense looked super sluggish yet again. Even with the win over Boston, the Warriors are 9-8 and 11th in the West standings. Things have gone sideways when you're looking up at everyone but the Pelicans, Clippers, Jazz and Kings.

According to recent reports, the Warriors' start to the season was fun while it lasted. Yaxel Lendeborg played great — and talked just as well — and immediately cemented himself in the starting lineup, not to mention the Rookie of the Year race. Even more encouraging, Stephen Curry looked like a vintage version of himself again after playing just 43 games a season ago. Through the first 11 games this year, Curry was second in the league in scoring behind only Luka Dončić. He appeared sharp and healthy — until he came out of the game in Houston in early November while holding his side after playing just six minutes. Turned out to be an abdominal tear. The Warriors announced that he would be reevaluated in two weeks, though the general ballpark for that kind of injury is closer to a month.

Not great, especially considering the Warriors were hardly at full strength as it was. Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody have yet to play a single minute while both recover from knee injuries. Meanwhile, Kristaps Porziņģis — who signed a new two-year deal worth $40 million in the offseason — is dealing with health issues and recently stepped away from basketball. Curry is the most critical piece of all, but not having several key components has left the Warriors painfully thin. That has reminded the Warriors how much tougher life is for all of them when Curry isn't on the floor and a rookie is suddenly tasked with leading the way.

It has been revealed that the recently ended losing streak included a stretch at San Antonio, New Orleans, Dallas and Memphis during which the average margin of defeat was more than 27 points. The loss to the Spurs was bad enough that Lendeborg came back with a new cut, prompting Steve Kerr to quip that the rookie dealt with the defeat by "[chopping] all his hair off.".

Through it all, Draymond hasn't been able to stop being Draymond. Green spent the run-up to the Celtics meeting warring with an NBA unc online, then got called for a tech while sitting on the bench during the game. Take a breath and go for a walk, man.

Industry observers note that curry can't return soon enough. If this goes on much longer, Yaxel and the rest of them will be fully bald.

PSV returned to the top of the Eredivisie with a thumping 5-2 win over Cambuur Leeuwarden as previous leaders Feyenoord lost a seven-goal thriller against the other Frisian club, Heerenveen.

It took just 46 seconds for PSV to get off the mark as Sven Mijnans headed in unmarked.

The midfielder added a second after 15 minutes and completed his hat-trick with a free-kick in the 80th minute to make the score 4-2, just as Cambuur were threatening a comeback.

According to recent reports, feyenoord’s dip in form continued as they let a two-goal lead slip at Heerenveen. The Rotterdammers looked to be in control going into the break with a trademark drilled shot by Anis Hadj Moussa and a penalty by Nacho Ferri.

But Maas Willemsen bundled in the ball from a corner on the stroke of half-time, before Ringo Meerveld came on for the second half and scored a hat-trick as Feyenoord’s defence crumbled under pressure.

In a recent development, “In the matches when we played well I saw a team that fought for each other,” Feyenoord coach Giovanni van Bronckhorst mentioned after the game. “Mentally strong, kept running even when we didn’t have the ball. That’s our strength. When we don’t do that we’re a lesser team.”.

Mexx Meerdink scored a hotly contested late penalty to settle a tempestuous game in Alkmaar as AZ came back from 3-1 down against Groningen to claim their first win in five matches.

Goalkeeper Etienne Vaessen was given a second yellow card for protesting too hard against the decision to penalise him for upending Ayoub Oufkir. Once the commotion died down Meerdink, who had missed from the spot against Vaessen earlier in the second half, made no mistake against substitute goalkeeper Lovro Stubljar.

Ajax missed the chance to take over top spot at Twente as their former striker Wout Weghorst scored a last-minute penalty to rescue a point for the home side.

Ajax had been 2-0 up with a bullet header by their giant striker Tolu Arokodare and a long-range strike by Rayane Bounida, before an own goal by Dies Janse brought the visitors back into the game.

In a recent development, fortuna Sittard also had to settle for a point against Telstar after going 2-0 up thanks to a bizarre own goal by Sem Valk. The defender’s sliced clearance looped over the head of Ronald Koeman Junior as the goalkeeper tried to head it away rather than risk being penalised for handling a backpass.

Goals just before half-time by Abdelnour Soualhia and Patrick Brouwer brought Telstar back into the game, but neither side was able to find a winner after the break.

That result allowed ADO, under the guidance of interim coach Levi Schwiebbe, to close the gap on 16th-placed Telstar to one point with a 3-1 win against Sparta, while bottom Willem II collected their third point of the season at home to PEC Zwolle.

ADO Den Haag 3-1 Sparta Rotterdam.

Cambuur Leeuwarden 2-5 PSV Eindhoven.
